data.title: The path to open-sourcing the DeepSeek inference engine
data.author: Palmik
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了DeepSeek团队将其内部推理引擎开源的计划和考虑。尽管之前在开源周活动中开源了一些库并获得了积极反馈，但开源整个推理引擎面临几个挑战，包括代码库差异、基础设施依赖和维护资源的限制。因此，团队决定通过与其他开源项目合作，模块化地贡献可重用组件和优化设计，而不是直接开源整个引擎。团队强调了对开源生态系统的感激，并承诺在新模型发布前与社区同步工程努力，以实现从 Day-0 起对最新硬件平台的支持。最终目标是建立一个同步的生态系统，使先进的AI能力能够在各种硬件平台上无缝实现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：DeepSeek和vLLM的技术进展、开源与商业利益的平衡、以及开源AI工具的战略意义

不同观点：
• **技术性能和改进空间**：ozgune指出vLLM通过采用DeepSeek论文中的改进，性能提升了3倍以上，但与DeepSeek的推理系统仍有差距，显示出进一步改进的潜力。
• **开源与社区贡献**：vintagedave赞扬了DeepSeek在面对技术障碍时仍选择与社区分享知识的做法，认为这是一种积极的贡献方式，即使并非所有信息都以完美整合的代码形式呈现。
• **商业公司开源动因**：avodonosov质疑商业AI公司为何分享研究成果，探讨了开源与商业利益之间的矛盾，并寻求合理解释。
• **开源但无维护的现实**：londons_explore建议公司即使无法长期维护代码，也应开源并说明情况，让社区有机会参与和改进。
• **DeepSeek的实际表现**：animal531基于个人使用经验，认为DeepSeek在代码生成方面的表现不如ChatGPT，存在较多问题，而ChatGPT在速度和质量上均有显著提升。
• **SaaS与自托管的选择**：gizmodo59表示尽管对本地运行AI工具感兴趣，但更倾向于使用SaaS以节省时间和精力，同时对ChatGPT的功能和性能表示满意。
• **开源AI工具的战略意义**：holoduke猜测中国大量发布开源AI工具可能是对抗美国技术主导地位的战略，认为这对市场有利。
• **DeepSeek与OpenAI的对比**：buyucu认为DeepSeek具备OpenAI声称的所有特点。
• **开源作为一种生存策略**：jeffrallen幽默地提出DeepSeek可能选择开源作为其GenAI发展的路径，类似于生物信息寻找新环境以繁殖自身。
• **代码重构的必要性**：rfoo简要总结了DeepSeek的现状，认为需要在公共视野下重建其vLLM分支。
• **开源与审查的关系**：nashashmi担心开源AI工具可能被用作实施审查的一种方式。

补充讨论：
• **知识共享的价值**：尽管技术实现存在障碍，社区贡献和知识共享仍被视为重要的进步动力。
• **商业逻辑与开源的平衡**：讨论中涉及商业公司为何选择开源其技术，反映了对商业利益和行业进步之间张力的思考。
• **开源工具的实际应用体验**：有用户基于个人使用经验对DeepSeek和ChatGPT的表现进行了对比，指出了实际应用中的问题和改进需求。

README.md
The Path to Open-Sourcing the DeepSeek Inference Engine
A few weeks ago,
during
Open Source Week
,
we open-sourced several libraries.
The response from the community has been incredibly positive - sparking inspiring collaborations, productive
discussions, and valuable bug fixes.
Encouraged by this, we’ve decided to take another step forward: contributing our internal inference engine back to the
open-source community.
We are deeply grateful for the open-source ecosystem, without which our progress toward AGI would not be possible.
Our training framework relies on
PyTorch
, and our inference engine is built
upon
vLLM
,
both of which have been instrumental in accelerating the training and deployment of DeepSeek models.
Given the growing demand for deploying models like
DeepSeek-V3
and
DeepSeek-R1
, we want to give back to the community as much as we can.
While we initially considered open-sourcing our full internal inference engine, we identified several challenges:
Codebase Divergence
: Our engine is based on an early fork of vLLM from over a year ago. Although structurally
similar, we’ve heavily customized it for DeepSeek models, making it difficult to extend for broader use cases.
Infrastructure Dependencies
: The engine is tightly coupled with our internal infrastructure, including cluster
management tools, making it impractical for public deployment without significant modifications.
Limited Maintenance Bandwidth
: As a small research team focused on developing better models, we lack bandwidth to
maintain a large open-source project.
Considering these challenges, we’ve decided to collaborate with existing open-source projects as more sustainable alternatives.
Moving forward, we will work closely with existing open-source projects to:
Extract Standalone Features
: Modularize and contribute reusable components as independent libraries.
Share Optimizations
: Contribute design improvements and implementation details directly.
We are profoundly grateful for the open-source movement - from operating systems and programming languages to machine
learning frameworks and inference engines. It’s an honor to contribute to this thriving ecosystem and to see our models
and code embraced by the community. Together, let’s push the boundaries of AGI and ensure its benefits serve all of
humanity.
Note
To clarify, this article outlines our approach to open-sourcing of our DeepSeek-Inference-Engine codebase only.
Regarding future model releases, we maintain an open and collaborative stance towards both the open-source community
and hardware partners.
We commit to proactively synchronizing inference-related engineering efforts prior to new model launches, with the
goal of enabling the community to achieve state-of-the-art (SOTA) support from Day-0. Our ultimate aim is to foster a
synchronized ecosystem where cutting-edge AI capabilities can be seamlessly implemented across diverse hardware
platforms upon official model releases.

data.title: Scientists: Protein IL-17 fights infection, acts on the brain, inducing anxiety
data.author: wglb
data.article_summary: 科学家发现免疫蛋白IL-17不仅能抵抗感染，还对大脑产生影响，引发焦虑或促进社交行为。麻省理工学院和哈佛医学院的研究显示，IL-17作用于大脑的两个区域：杏仁核和体感皮层，产生不同效果。在杏仁核中，IL-17引发焦虑；而在体感皮层，它促进社交行为。这些研究表明免疫系统和神经系统紧密相连。研究还发现，IL-17通过其受体IL-17RA和IL-17RB影响大脑功能，可能最初是作为神经调节剂进化而来，后来被免疫系统用于促发炎症。这项研究揭示了免疫分子如何影响情绪和行为，提供了对身心状态联系的新理解。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：免疫系统、炎症与抑郁症等精神健康问题之间的关联

不同观点：
• **eveningsteps** 提出，抑制IL-17蛋白（如使用bimekizumab）不仅能缓解牛皮癣症状，还能在长时间内改善情绪。该评论通过实验治疗项目中的观察支持这一观点，指出免疫调节可能对抑郁症有影响。

• **elia_42** 支持免疫系统与大脑之间双向沟通的观点，强调免疫系统不仅抵御病原体，还通过细胞因子与大脑沟通以保护个体及群体。该评论基于个人经历，认为免疫激活期间情绪变化是常见的。

• **funnym0nk3y** 认为抑郁症的病因复杂，包括脑网络、早期生活逆境、睡眠障碍等因素，并提出炎症假说。虽然承认炎症与抑郁症有关，但质疑炎症的起源及其治疗的目标，指出SSRIs的抗炎作用可能是下游效应，而非直接作用。

• **jujube69** 引用研究，指出维生素缺乏与抑郁症及IL-17水平之间的关系，并列举了如CoQ10、叶酸等可能降低IL-17水平的维生素。该评论强调通过调整血液水平来改善抑郁症的可能性。

• **mleonhard** 提供相关研究，讨论免疫系统触发焦虑的机制，并提出N-乙酰半胱氨酸（NAC）作为治疗精神障碍的新方法，认为其具有抗炎作用且相对安全。

• **chaps** 分享个人经历，指出全身炎症与间歇性恐慌发作之间的关联，认为这进一步证实了炎症与心理健康问题之间的相关性。

• **fsckboy** 警告不要过度依赖化学治疗，提出这种免疫系统反应可能是适应性的，旨在避免个体在生病时参与危险活动。担心现代医学干预可能带来不良副作用或削弱免疫反应。

补充讨论：
• **ashoeafoot** 以讽刺口吻提出抑郁症可能是一种自我隔离机制。
• **jagaerglad** 分享个人观察，认为发烧后感觉更好可能与免疫系统的作用有关。
• **idontwantthis** 提问IL-17蛋白与血清素之间的关系，以及SSRIs的效果是否与此相关。
• **bitwize** 提供维基百科链接，指出“疾病行为”可能与讨论相关，进一步探讨免疫系统对行为的影响。

争议焦点：
• 免疫系统对心理健康问题的直接影响及其治疗的有效性和安全性。部分评论担心现代医学干预可能带来的副作用，而另一些评论则支持通过免疫调节来改善情绪和心理状态。

Scientists discover the protein IL-17 that fights infection also acts on the brain, inducing anxiety or sociability
by
Massachusetts Institute of Technology
Credit: Andrew Neel from Pexels
Immune molecules called cytokines play important roles in the body's defense against infection, helping to control inflammation and coordinating the responses of other immune cells. A growing body of evidence suggests that some of these molecules also influence the brain, leading to behavioral changes during illness.
Two new studies from MIT and Harvard Medical School, focusing on a cytokine called IL-17, now add to that evidence. The researchers found that IL-17 acts on two distinct brain regions—the amygdala and the somatosensory cortex—to exert two divergent effects. In the amygdala, IL-17 can elicit feelings of anxiety, while in the cortex it promotes sociable behavior.
These findings suggest that the immune and nervous systems are tightly interconnected, says Gloria Choi, an associate professor of brain and cognitive sciences, a member of MIT's Picower Institute for Learning and Memory, and one of the senior authors of the studies.
"If you're sick, there's so many more things that are happening to your internal states, your mood, and your behavioral states, and that's not simply you being fatigued physically. It has something to do with the brain," she says.
Jun Huh, an associate professor of immunology at Harvard Medical School, is also a senior author of both studies, which appear in
Cell
. One of the papers was led by Picower Institute Research Scientist Byeongjun Lee and former Picower Institute research scientist Jeong-Tae Kwon, and the other was led by Harvard Medical School postdoc Yunjin Lee and Picower Institute postdoc Tomoe Ishikawa.
Behavioral effects
Choi and Huh became interested in IL-17 several years ago, when they found it was involved in a phenomenon known as the fever effect. Large-scale studies of autistic children have found that for many of them, their behavioral symptoms temporarily diminish when they have a fever.
In a
2019 study
in mice, Choi and Huh showed that in some cases of infection, IL-17 is released and suppresses a small region of the brain's cortex known as S1DZ. Overactivation of neurons in this region can lead to autism-like behavioral symptoms in mice, including repetitive behaviors and reduced sociability.
"This molecule became a link that connects immune system activation, manifested as a fever, to changes in
brain function
and changes in the animals' behavior," Choi says.
IL-17 comes in six different forms, and there are five different receptors that can bind to it.
In their two new papers, the researchers set out to map which of these receptors are expressed in different parts of the brain. This mapping revealed that a pair of receptors known as IL-17RA and IL-17RB is found in the cortex, including in the S1DZ region that the researchers had previously identified. The receptors are located in a population of neurons that receive proprioceptive input and are involved in controlling behavior.
When a type of IL-17 known as IL-17E binds to these receptors, the neurons become less excitable, which leads to the behavioral effects seen in the 2019 study.
"IL-17E, which we've shown to be necessary for behavioral mitigation, actually does act almost exactly like a neuromodulator in that it will immediately reduce these neurons' excitability," Choi says.
"So, there is an immune molecule that's acting as a neuromodulator in the brain, and its main function is to regulate excitability of neurons."
Choi hypothesizes that IL-17 may have originally evolved as a neuromodulator, and later on was appropriated by the immune system to play a role in promoting inflammation.
That idea is consistent with previous work showing that in the worm C. elegans, IL-17 has no role in the immune system but instead acts on neurons. Among its effects in worms, IL-17 promotes aggregation, a form of social behavior. Additionally, in mammals, IL-17E is actually made by neurons in the cortex, including S1DZ.
"There's a possibility that a couple of forms of IL-17 perhaps evolved first and foremost to act as a neuromodulator in the brain, and maybe later were hijacked by the immune system also to act as immune modulators," Choi says.
Provoking anxiety
In the other
Cell
paper, the researchers explored another brain location where they found IL-17 receptors—the amygdala. This almond-shaped structure plays an important role in processing emotions, including fear and anxiety.
That study revealed that in a region known as the basolateral amygdala (BLA), the IL-17RA and IL-17RE receptors, which work as a pair, are expressed in a discrete popula

data.title: Tariff: A Python package that imposes tariffs on Python imports
data.author: khaledh
data.article_summary: "Tariff" 是一个恶搞性质的Python包，版本1.0.0，由Python Economist开发，旨在通过引入"关税"机制来减慢特定外部库的导入速度。用户可以设置如numpy、pandas等库的关税百分比，导入时这些库将被故意延迟相应时间，以模拟加征关税的效果。该包带有政治讽刺色彩，使用MIT许可证，目前处于Alpha开发阶段，仅供娱乐，使用需谨慎。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个可能自动施加关税的编程工具的评论和不同观点

不同观点：
• [支持与功能请求] **Lvl999Noob** 建议该工具应自动识别包裹来源国并施加当时的关税，同时判断开发者是否在美国境内外，认为中等努力实现即可。
• [支持与扩展建议] **elashri** 支持默认对所有包裹施加10%的基础关税，即使从不存在的地方（如企鹅岛）进口。
• [讽刺/反对态度] **outer_web** 讽刺地表示这个工具会激励他们从零开始编写所有代码，暗示不支持这种复杂的工具。
• [批评与惩罚观点] **graemep** 希望通过该工具惩罚添加过多依赖的开发者。
• [中立/反对政治介入] **JodieBenitez** 表示自己不是美国人，不想在编程工具中看到政治观点，认为开发者应避免在编程工具中表达政治意见。

补充讨论：
• [幽默回应] **norskeld** 用图片和代码幽默回应，暗示某些包可能会有例外情况（如numpy设为-100关税）。
• [信息补充] **3eb7988a1663** 提供了相关项目的问题追踪和拉取请求链接，为讨论添加了技术背景。
• [批评与讽刺] **hughdbrown** 讽刺地表示某些包在“欺骗”他们。
• [困惑与娱乐] **Imustaskforhelp** 表示不理解关税如何应用于编程，但认为这个工具的创造很有趣，是一种政治与编程的结合。
• [中立但思考] **moktonar** 认为这个想法可能并不像看起来那么愚蠢，暗示可能有潜在价值。
• [疑问] **akkartik** 提出“什么是#mipa？”，表明讨论中可能涉及一些未解释的术语或概念。

争议焦点：
- 是否应在编程工具中自动施加关税，支持者认为可以默认施加，而反对者则认为这可能增加不必要的复杂性。
- 编程工具中是否应包含政治观点，部分开发者（如JodieBenitez）明确表示反对，认为工具应保持中立。

Project description
👊 TARIFF 🔥
The GREATEST, most TREMENDOUS Python package that makes importing great again!
About
TARIFF is a fantastic tool that lets you impose import tariffs on Python packages. We're going to bring manufacturing BACK to your codebase by making foreign imports more EXPENSIVE!
Installation
pip
install
tariff
Usage
import
tariff
# Set your tariff rates (package_name: percentage)
tariff
.
set
({
"numpy"
:
50
,
# 50% tariff on numpy
"pandas"
:
200
,
# 200% tariff on pandas
"requests"
:
150
# 150% tariff on requests
})
# Now when you import these packages, they'll be TARIFFED!
import
numpy
# This will be 50% slower
import
pandas
# This will be 200% slower
How It Works
When you import a package that has a tariff:
TARIFF measures how long the original import takes
TARIFF makes the import take longer based on your tariff percentage
TARIFF announces the tariff with a TREMENDOUS message
Example Output
JUST IMPOSED a 50% TARIFF on numpy! Original import took 45000 us, now takes 67500 us. American packages are WINNING AGAIN! #MIPA
Why TARIFF?
Because foreign packages have been STEALING our CPU cycles for TOO LONG! It's time to put AMERICA FIRST and make importing FAIR and BALANCED again!
License
This is a parody package. Use at your own risk. MAKE IMPORTING GREAT AGAIN!

data.title: Tomb Engine
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: Tomb Engine 1.8.1是一款用于定制《古墓丽影》冒险的开源引擎，是一个与Core Design、Eidos Interactive或Embracer Group AB无关的社区项目。该引擎的代码是开源的，旨在鼓励贡献和用于学习目的，不得出售。开发者不对源代码的非法使用负责，且该项目由非付费贡献者在业余时间维护。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Tomb Raider粉丝项目、引擎开发及相关法律问题的讨论

不同观点：
• simonsarris分享了自己早期制作Tomb Raider关卡的经历，强调了创造过程的魅力，并提到Minecraft和购买土地作为类似体验的延续。
• jbreckmckye对如何开始像重新实现Tomb Raider这样的项目表示好奇，认为这涉及大量的逆向工程和试错。
• elpocko指出网站上没有清楚提供开源代码的链接，经过编辑后找到了GitHub上的源码链接。
• keyle认为关卡编辑器与引擎同样重要，并分享了一个相关的编辑器项目链接，强调了开放源码编辑器对游戏设计的重要性。
• sho_hn介绍了另一个相关的项目TRX，并分享了自己对MacOS和Web端口的工作经验，强调了社区的贡献。
• recursive对网站声明“TombEngine不得出售”表示赞赏，认为这增加了对项目的信任。
• pull_my_finger提到在游戏领域已经有一个同名引擎（ToME），认为这可能会引起混淆。
• omneity对项目可能引发的新的游戏类型或社区表示期待，并提出了可能的创意组合。
• wincy分享了自己与姐妹和朋友玩Tomb Raider 2的美好回忆，特别提到了一些有趣的游戏时刻。
• zanellato19认为这个项目可以用来制作类似Armored Core的游戏。
• paulryanrogers表示一直在关注Discord上的项目进展，认为粉丝项目让游戏走向了发行商不会选择的方向。
• philipwhiuk质疑项目使用的资产是否经过合法授权，预测项目可能会遇到法律问题。
• reassess_blind指出网站上缺乏游戏截图，怀疑这是为了掩盖知识产权侵权。
• rlexsu抱怨网站首页的视频没有展示引擎功能，只是播放了背景音乐。

补充讨论：
• 项目合法性问题是一个争议焦点，部分用户质疑项目是否会遭遇知识产权问题。
• 不同用户对项目的创意潜力和未来发展方向有不同的期待和设想。
• 技术实现和社区贡献是另一个值得注意的讨论点，特别是涉及逆向工程和多平台支持的问题。

整个讨论围绕技术实现、法律问题、创意潜力和社区贡献展开，展示了多角度的看法和关注点。

data.title: Behind the 6-digit code: Building HOTP and TOTP from scratch
data.author: dogacel
data.article_summary:
这篇文章主要介绍了基于一次性密码（OTP）的认证机制，特别是HOTP和TOTP的工作原理。OTP是一种用于动态生成密码的技术，有效防止重放攻击。与传统密码不同，OTP每次使用后即失效，或在限定时间内有效。

文章首先解释了OTP的基本概念，然后详细介绍了HOTP（基于计数器的一次性密码）和TOTP（基于时间的一次性密码）。HOTP通过一个递增的计数器生成密码，而TOTP则使用当前时间作为计数器，通常以30秒为间隔更新密码。

文章进一步说明了TOTP的生成公式，强调了密码生成依赖于共享的密钥，且该算法必须是可预测且同步的，以确保客户端和服务器生成相同的密码。TOTP的优势在于利用时间同步，避免了计数器同步问题，并减少了恶意用户收集密码的可能性。

文章最后提到，HOTP和TOTP已被标准化，并广泛用于双因素认证（2FA）系统中。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：TOTP及HOTP等一次性密码技术的工作原理、应用场景及其实施细节

不同观点：
• ucarion认为，"忘记密码"流程中的六位验证码虽然是一次性密码（OTP），但不属于HOTP或TOTP，因为没有像TOTP那样通过QR码注册密钥的步骤。他还提出可以用公钥加密代替HMAC，并指出WebAuthn已经实现类似概念。此外，他还提醒要防范暴力破解。
• 3eb7988a1663提供了简短的Python实现以帮助理解TOTP原理，并分享了一个20行代码的GitHub链接。
• sksxihve质疑为什么银行仍然使用短信2FA而不是TOTP，并询问是否存在监管问题。
• Steve6分享了自己创建API生成TOTP码的经验，并提供了一个用于测试的API链接（https://totpapi.com），希望能帮助其他人。
• notpushkin怀疑Facebook在密码恢复时使用的是随机生成的数字，而不是基于HOTP/TOTP的方案。
• gbraad分享了自己使用zsh、openssl和xxd创建的命令行TOTP工具，并提到11年前曾为诺基亚手机开发过类似应用。
• yuliyp确认Facebook的登录/账户恢复码不是TOTP/HOTP，而是随机数，并建议通过解码QR码来验证实现。
• DarkCrusader2提供了另一篇关于TOTP的简洁文章链接。
• ryandv推荐了RFC 4226和RFC 6238作为学习TOTP和HOTP的入门资料，并提到自己曾用Rust实现过这些标准。
• thatkid02提供了自己关于JavaScript双因素认证的文章链接。
• rothfuss对文章中的时钟问题感到困惑，并质疑文章中的图片是否为AI生成。
• coppsilgold建议在账户上设置TOTP以获得更好的待遇，并提到一些密码管理器（如KeepassXC）集成了TOTP功能，但也指出这可能在某些情况下违背2FA的初衷。

补充讨论：
• 对TOTP和HOTP的实现细节存在不同理解，尤其在密钥注册和随机数生成方面。
• 有人提到银行继续使用短信2FA可能涉及监管问题，但未有明确答案。
• 对Facebook在密码恢复过程中使用随机数而非TOTP的怀疑引发了对具体实现的讨论。
• 提供了一些实用工具和代码实现以帮助理解和应用TOTP技术。
• 对文章内容（如时钟问题和图片质量）的批评和疑问。

43653322.article_content:
A while ago, I have started working on authorization and authentication at work. This taught me a lot about how modern authentication systems work. However I have always thought One-Time Password logins are the most mystical ones. A six-digit code that changes every time and can be used to verify your identity. How does the server know the newly generated one, and how is it really secure? In this post, I will explain what HOTP, TOTP is and how they work by sharing my own implementation from scratch.
A sample OTP login code
What Are OTPs
?
One-Time Passwords (OTPs) are a widely-used form of authentication. You’ve likely encountered them when using a “Secure Login” app like Google Authenticator, or during a “Forgot Password” flow where a temporary code is sent to your email or phone.
Unlike traditional passwords, OTPs are only valid for a single use or a limited time window. This greatly reduces the risk of password replay attacks, where someone captures the password used to login and tries to reuse it.
Passwords can be used repeatedly. When leaked, malicious actors can impersonate the user and access critical information.
Like the traditional password authentication approach, the user and the authority (server) still needs to agree on a common secret key. During the regular password authentication, this secret key is directly communicated to the authority. There are many ways of doing this process safely, such as hashing the password or sending it over an encrypted network. However the risk still exists, as the password itself never changes, as long as we use our devices to type our passwords, there is some way those malicious actors can watch and get that information before it reaching the network.
So instead of using a constant secret key, we can use something dynamic that changes over time. As a simple example, assume when those two people first met, they have set their secretly hidden clocks to a random time together.
Using secret clocks as a basic OTP implementation
Also in some examples like Facebook's password recovery, this secret clock is not shared with the user directly but rather server's generated one-time password is sent via a trusted medium, such as an email to the user.
Obviously a clock on its own is not secure, as in this example Plankton could have predicted the time-shift of the secret clock based on the real time. However for the sake of this example, I wanted to show how copying the "password" is not enough on its own. Let's take a look at some strategies to build this "secret clock" and make sure it is not possible to predict time just by knowing a single code in some point in time.
There are two common types of OTP algorithms:
HOTP (HMAC-based One-Time Password)
– based on a counter that increments every time an OTP is requested.
TOTP (Time-based One-Time Password)
– based on the current time, typically using 30-second intervals.
These methods are standardized in
RFC 4226
(for HOTP) and
RFC 6238
(for TOTP), and are used in many modern 2FA (two-factor authentication) implementations.
A counter based password method is easier to understand. Imagine two people met and generated a totally random series of numbers. They both start from count 0, as in each attempt, user needs to communicate to the server with the secret key in the given index. However this comes with several problems,
Clients needs to sync their counter, if there is a skew, they might get temporarily locked out.
Malicious actors can collect upcoming login codes by phishing the user and those codes can be used for a long time.
Therefore, instead of storing a counter, we can use the current time as the counter. That's how TOTP works. Using time makes synchronization easier, as many modern machines already use technologies such as NTP to sync their time and this prevents malicious actors from harvesting codes as their code will be valid for only next 30 seconds or so, not for a long sequence of future login attempts.
How to Generate TOTPs?
The analogy of two people met and decided on a totally random series of numbers is partially realistic. However it is not feasible to have such a huge list, you potentially need to have millions of secret numbers to support OTPs for a reasonable time. Therefore we should use algorithms that are cryptographically  safe that generate values based on a secret key. It is important that this algorithm is not random, as both user and the authority will hold a copy of this secret key and they should be able to generate the same value given the same time.
We have introduced HOTP first because the actual implementation of TOTPs are actually HOTP based. Instead of using a static counter, TOTPs use the time as the current counter.  We can write the following formula to find the counter in any given time,
\[ c(t) = \left\lfloor \frac{t - t_0}{X} \right\rfloor \]
Here \(t_0\) is the starting time, in most systems this is the default UNIX epoch timestamp, 1 January 1970. \(X\) is the period you want the
43653322.article_summary:
这篇文章主要介绍了基于一次性密码（OTP）的认证机制，特别是HOTP和TOTP的工作原理。OTP是一种用于动态生成密码的技术，有效防止重放攻击。与传统密码不同，OTP每次使用后即失效，或在限定时间内有效。

文章首先解释了OTP的基本概念，然后详细介绍了HOTP（基于计数器的一次性密码）和TOTP（基于时间的一次性密码）。HOTP通过一个递增的计数器生成密码，而TOTP则使用当前时间作为计数器，通常以30秒为间隔更新密码。

文章进一步说明了TOTP的生成公式，强调了密码生成依赖于共享的密钥，且该算法必须是可预测且同步的，以确保客户端和服务器生成相同的密码。TOTP的优势在于利用时间同步，避免了计数器同步问题，并减少了恶意用户收集密码的可能性。

文章最后提到，HOTP和TOTP已被标准化，并广泛用于双因素认证（2FA）系统中。

data.title: Laser Launch into Orbit
data.author: EA-3167
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了激光发射系统作为一种突破传统火箭性能限制的潜在解决方案。传统化学燃料火箭的性能受限于燃料能量，而核能和电动火箭也面临重量和能量输出问题。激光发射系统通过将能量源从火箭上分离，由地面激光器提供能量加热推进剂，理论上可实现700到10000秒的比冲（Isp），且无需携带反应堆或高能化学品，使火箭更小、更安全、更便宜，发射成本可降至每公斤1到100美元。然而，激光系统面临效率损失问题，尤其是激光生成器的效率较低（约25%），大气层也会吸收部分激光能量。最佳方案是使用光纤激光器，通过大气窗口波长（如光学或微波波长）传输能量，以减少损失。尽管存在挑战，激光发射系统有望大幅降低太空进入成本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：激光推进技术及其在航天发射和空间活动中的应用

不同观点：
• **支持激光推进技术的潜力**：
  - **[nickfromseattle]** 分享了20世纪90年代利用激光技术提升小型原型机几米的视频，并引用了Leik Myrabo的相关研究，显示了对该技术可行性的信心。
  - **[Cthulhu_]** 提供了Atomic Rockets / Project Rho的相关文章链接，进一步探讨了激光推进的数学和理论基础。

• **质疑激光推进技术的实际可行性和经济性**：
  - **[os2warpman]** 通过计算指出，使用激光热引擎发射50吨火箭需要超过2GW的激光功率，实际需要的电力可能高达5.5至18GW，质疑这种技术在经济性和工程实现上的可行性。
  - **[notahacker]** 认为高功率激光推进技术在太空外部、无大气环境下更有意义，但在地球上应用面临功率传递和大气干扰等问题，且目前公开演示的成果不显著。

• **激光推进的其他潜在应用**：
  - **[andrewflnr]** 提出激光逆向推进可用于减缓从太空降落的材料的速度，并讨论了用廉价材料包裹高价值载荷的可能性。
  - **[sevensor]** 担心高能量激光在大气层中会产生等离子体，影响推进效率。

• **创新想法和工程挑战**：
  - **[bilsbie]** 提出使用高电压（如兆伏级）轻质电线为火箭提供能量的设想，认为这可能作为低速第一阶段的解决方案。
  - **[bdamm]** 认为这些想法很酷但实际可行性尚不明确，指出空间产业的价值可能推动此类研究。

• **历史和文化视角**：
  - **[ben_w]** 分享了自己20年前关于使用定日镜聚焦热交换器的想法，并指出类似项目的工程难度，如燃料成本和设备耐受性。
  - **[salynchnew]** 提到《The Millennial Project》一书，对没有亿万富翁将激光推进作为个人 passion project 表示惊讶。

补充讨论：
• 对已故激光专家Jordin Kare的缅怀（**[pfdietz]**）。
• 对纤维激光器技术的质疑（**[lupusreal]**），认为百束小激光通过光纤合并成大束激光的想法不正确。

争议焦点：
• 激光推进技术在实际应用中的可行性与经济性，特别是在地面应用时如何有效传递高能量并避免大气干扰。

In this post, we will look at laser launch systems, how they would look like and perform, and how they might be applied to reach orbit and beyond.
The advantages of laser launch
140GHz is microwave.
A typical rocket engine does two things: deliver propellant and heat it up using an energy source.
In a chemical-fuel rocket, the propellant is combustible and is burned in a combustion chamber. The resulting heat and gasses serve both as propellant and an energy source. In a nuclear thermal rocket, the propellant is inert and nuclear material is used to heat it up. An electric rocket uses internal power, derived from a nuclear reactor or solar panels, to accelerate inert propellant using electrostatic or electromagnetic effects.
What temperature do you think the gasses inside the nozzle are at?
The performance of a rocket is limited by how much energy can be delivered to the propellant. This is how much energy is released by the combustion of fuels such as liquid hydrogen or kerosene, how much heat is released by a nuclear core of how much electricity is delivered to an electric rocket.
However, rocket fuel is only so energetic, and there are strict limits on how hot a nuclear core can get before it starts melting down or has to be designed larger and heavier. Electric engines are rather low on specific power, and the more the rocket consumes, the more mass has to be dedicated to producing energy.
Liquid fuelled rockets are a mature technology that have pretty much reached the limits of chemical performance. For example, the
SSME Plus
was designed for an Isp of 467 seconds (4580m/s exhaust velocity), and the
Rocketdyne AEC
engine with 481 seconds (4718m/s exhaust velocity). This is very near the theoretical maximum for liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen (about 500s). Going slightly further requires impractical fluoride oxidizers.
Nuclear rockets can push the envelope, but testing of solid-core designs delivered low Isp at high thrust levels, or high isp but low thrust in vacuum. Gaseous core rockets can provide both high thrust and high isp, but they require decades of research.
Electric rockets have similar problems. Nuclear reactors in space are very heavy, and solar panels do not provide enough energy to lift off the Earth.
The solution is to separate the energy source from the spaceship.
A Skylon variant where energy for heating the hydrogen propellant is provided by laser beam.
Laser beams can deliver the output of a several-thousand-ton power plants on the ground to the engine, at no extra cost. Although the specifics depend on the designs being used, the performance of laser-powered rockets ranges from 700 to 10000 seconds, with no upper limit except for laser power levels.
A combination of high Isp and powerful engines that do not require on-board reactors, nuclear materials or volatile chemicals makes for small, cheap and safe rockets. The price per kilo in orbit can be made manageable at $1 to $100 per kg, therefore opening up access to space.
The problems to solve
Naturally, a rocket going into space cannot carry along an electrical wire to the ground to deliver energy. A power plant on the ground generates electricity, which is used to power a laser generator. The beam is then focused onto the spaceship, where an engine uses the laser energy directly, or absorbs it as heat indirectly.
Four rough approaches to using laser power in a rocket
The intermediary steps between the power plant's electrical energy and the spaceship's engine create efficiency losses. The biggest loss is in the laser itself. Laser generators are quite an inefficient piece of technology. Conventional lasers, such as solid-state lasers, have an efficiency of about 25%. Pure diode lasers can reach over 60% efficiency, but cannot generate intense pulses. Pulsed lasers have to rely on flash-pumping technology, which gives mediocre 0.1% to 5% efficiency.
Fibre laser configuration from a cutting machine.
Fibre lasers, where hundreds of tiny beams are joined through optical fibres into a larger beam, have both high efficiency, high resistance to heat and high pulsed power output, so are the best solution for a laser launch system.
Another source of losses is from the laser beam travelling through the atmosphere. Some of it
is absorbed
. The best wavelengths for focusing a laser on a spaceship, such as ultraviolet (<400nm wavelength) do not travel far through the atmosphere. Optical wavelengths (700 to 400nm) and infrared to microwave wavelengths (700nm to 1cm) have narrow 'atmospheric windows' where they can travel through air without being quickly absorbed. Even so, a few percent is lost when the laser beam traverse dozens of kilometers of water vapour and various gasses.
The 'atmospheric window' wavelengths
If there is a heavy cloud cover, optical wavelengths will not go through. Microwave beams are the only solution, as they are the least affected by clouds and water vapour.

data.title: Show HN: Portable Giant File Viewer
data.author: sunny41
data.article_summary: Giant Log Viewer 是一个跨平台的桌面便携应用程序，用于在 `less` 不可用的环境下查看任意大小的文本文件。它能够快速加载文件，且内存占用低，无论文件是 4 MB、4 GB 还是 4 TB，只要不超过某些限制（如 JVM 堆内存最多 80 MB）。该工具支持 UTF-8 和 ASCII 编码文件，但有一些限制，如不支持过长的行（≥ 1 MB）、表情符号显示不全、以及仅支持 Windows、macOS 和 Linux 系统。用户可以通过拖放文件到应用界面进行查看，并使用类似 `less` 的键盘导航。当前版本还有一些不足，如可执行文件未由验证开发者签名。项目源代码托管在 GitHub，欢迎贡献和反馈。

Giant Log Viewer
Needing to check a 4.9 GB log file on a platform where the
less
file pager is not available? Don't cry. This software is going to save you!
This software loads instantly with same low memory footprint regardless of a 4 MB, 4 GB or 4 TB text file is opened, as long as it doesn't hit any
limitation
. The JVM is limited to use at most 80 MB heap memory (plus overheads) currently.
Limitations
Supports UTF-8 encoding and ASCII text files only
Doesn't work if there is a long line (>= 1 MB) in the file
Emoji sequences are not supported -- it would be displayed as multiple emoji characters
Doesn't work if your OS has no GUI
Doesn't work if you are not using Windows, macOS nor Linux
Not as powerful as
less
yet
How to Use
Drag and drop a UTF-8 / ASCII text file to this application.
Navigate with a keyboard. The
less
key bindings can be used. Click the "?" button in the top-right corner for the full keymap.
Executables are not signed by verified developers
Builds are built by GitHub runners which take the source code published here directly. You can always examine the source code or build yourself. Please also consider donation so that I could sign the executables one day.
Bug Reporting
https://github.com/sunny-chung/giant-log-viewer/issues
Contributions
Welcome! Note that this project is
slightly reluctant to use third-party libraries
.
About
A cross-platform desktop portable application that allows viewing text files of any size when `less` is not available.

43661939.article_summary: Giant Log Viewer 是一个跨平台的桌面便携应用程序，用于在 `less` 不可用的环境下查看任意大小的文本文件。它能够快速加载文件，且内存占用低，无论文件是 4 MB、4 GB 还是 4 TB，只要不超过某些限制（如 JVM 堆内存最多 80 MB）。该工具支持 UTF-8 和 ASCII 编码文件，但有一些限制，如不支持过长的行（≥ 1 MB）、表情符号显示不全、以及仅支持 Windows、macOS 和 Linux 系统。用户可以通过拖放文件到应用界面进行查看，并使用类似 `less` 的键盘导航。当前版本还有一些不足，如可执行文件未由验证开发者签名。项目源代码托管在 GitHub，欢迎贡献和反馈。
43661939.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：文件管理工具及其功能特性

不同观点：
• [quyse] 支持使用 Far Manager，认为其优点在于能够查看任意大小的文件而无需加载到内存中，并且支持编码和搜索功能，处理二进制文件时表现良好。他还提供了Far Manager的官方链接。
• [zemlyansky] 提出了一个基于浏览器的替代方案，使用了JavaScript和流技术，并提供了一个链接，但该链接可能存在问题。
• [cmiller1] 回应了[zemlyansky]的建议，指出所提供的链接无法访问，出现了访问受限的错误。
• [knowitnone] 提到"Less"工具也可以下载使用，虽然提出了不同的工具，但表达了对当前讨论工具的认可。
• [sunny41] 提到了AI的热门趋势，并指出该工具的图标是使用AI生成的，试图将AI技术引入讨论。
• [atmanactive] 关注工具的界面定制性，特别是颜色和深色模式是否可以调整，暗示了对用户界面个性化需求的关注。

补充讨论：
• 链接的有效性问题：[zemlyansky]提供的浏览器工具链接无法访问，[cmiller1]指出了这个问题。
• 工具的界面定制性：[atmanactive]对工具的颜色和深色模式提出了疑问，显示出用户对界面可定制性的关注。
• 对AI技术的提及：[sunny41]将AI技术与工具的图标设计联系起来，虽然这与主要讨论点关系不大，但显示了AI技术在当前软件工具讨论中的热度。

争议焦点：
• 工具链接的有效性：[zemlyansky]提供的浏览器工具链接无法访问，[cmiller1]指出了这一问题，这使得该替代方案的实用性受到质疑。

总结：讨论主要围绕文件管理工具的功能和特性展开，参与者提出了多个工具并讨论了它们的优缺点，同时涉及了工具链接的有效性和界面定制性等问题。

data.title: Teuken-7B-Base and Teuken-7B-Instruct: Towards European LLMs (2024)
data.author: doener
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了两款多语言大语言模型——Teuken-7B-Base和Teuken-7B-Instruct，旨在支持欧盟24种官方语言，促进欧洲语言多样性。模型训练数据中约60%为非英语数据，并使用自定义的多语言分词器，解决了现有大语言模型主要关注英语或少数高资源语言的局限性。文章详细介绍了模型的开发原则，包括数据组成、分词器优化和训练方法。模型在多语言基准测试中表现出色，在欧洲版本的ARC、HellaSwag、MMLU和TruthfulQA等测试中性能优异。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：多语言大语言模型的性能和应用

不同观点：
• [ozgune] 提到在使用多语言LLM（如Llama 3.3 70B）时，发现模型对英语问题的回答质量较高，而对土耳其语的回答质量较差。然而，如果先将土耳其语问题翻译成英语，获得答案后再翻译回土耳其语，回答质量会显著提高。这表明通过翻译可以提升非英语问题的表现。

• [KronisLV] 支持EuroLLM项目，认为它在处理拉脱维亚语等欧洲语言方面表现优异，优于其他同类模型如Llama和Qwen。

• [JKolios] 认为Mistral的模型在处理较不常用的欧洲语言方面表现良好，暗示在LLM领域中，Mistral已经提供了不错的多样性选择。

• [denimboy] 提出RWKV-V5 7B模型与讨论主题的比较，并提供相关博客链接供参考。

• [NKosmatos] 提到2024年发布的希腊LLM——Meltemi，并提供相关链接，强调其在希腊语言处理上的优势。

补充讨论：
• [tannhaeuser] 讨论了Mistral AI在巴黎的背景，认为其模型性能优异，特别是在与Llama3.1和Qwen2.5等模型比较时。还提到在获取资本和人才方面的地域差异，但认为这不影响最终模型性能。

• [andai] 对预训练过程中减少英语文本以平衡性能的策略提出疑问，担心这会损害其他基准测试的表现。

• [miros_love] 对欧洲版本的基准测试（如EU-ARC）提出质疑，认为不应仅仅依赖这些基准测试，并建议在处理低资源语言时应纳入更多相关语言。

• [htrp] 提到欧洲版本的基准测试如ARC、HellaSwag、MMLU和TruthfulQA，显示出对多样化基准测试的关注。

• [smokel] 对一篇语言论文中的语法错误提出批评，认为这影响了论文的可信度。

• [YetAnotherNick] 比较了Llama 3.1、Qwen 2.5和Gemma 3的性能，认为Llama 3.1在欧洲MMLU等任务上的表现不如其他模型。

争议焦点：多语言LLM在不同语言上的表现差异以及如何有效评估和提升这些模型的性能。特别是在非英语语言（如土耳其语、希腊语、拉脱维亚语等）上的表现优劣和基准测试的合理性。

Abstract:
We present two multilingual LLMs designed to embrace Europe's linguistic diversity by supporting all 24 official languages of the European Union. Trained on a dataset comprising around 60% non-English data and utilizing a custom multilingual tokenizer, our models address the limitations of existing LLMs that predominantly focus on English or a few high-resource languages. We detail the models' development principles, i.e., data composition, tokenizer optimization, and training methodologies. The models demonstrate competitive performance across multilingual benchmarks, as evidenced by their performance on European versions of ARC, HellaSwag, MMLU, and TruthfulQA.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对小说《Lolita》的理解和读者的反应

不同观点：
• [cafard的观点]  
  - 认为《Lolita》并没有让读者对恋童癖的心理有深入了解。  
  - 指出小说中虽然叙述者偶尔提到背后的阴暗面，但整体上并未深入揭示这一问题。

• [fifticon的观点]  
  - 认为公众对这本书的愤怒与他们对书籍的阅读和理解程度成反比。  
  - 暗示那些对书内容了解不多或理解不深的人更容易表达愤怒。

补充讨论：
• [争议的焦点]  
  - 争议在于《Lolita》是否让读者对恋童癖的心理有深入了解，以及公众对该书内容的反应是否基于充分的理解。
  
• [论据和例子]  
  - cafard提到自己多年前读过这本书，并基于个人阅读体验认为小说并没有提供对恋童癖心理的深刻洞察。  
  - fifticon则指出，许多对该书表达愤怒的人可能并没有深入阅读或理解其内容，暗示这种反应可能是不恰当的或基于误解。

• [讨论的关系]  
  - cafard从个人角度出发，分享了对小说内容的看法，而fifticon则更关注公众对该书的普遍反应及其背后的原因，两者从不同角度讨论了同一主题。

data.title: Whistleblower details how DOGE may have taken sensitive NLRB data
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 一篇报道披露，根据一名举报人的指控，特朗普政府效率部门（DOGE）的一个团队可能获取并隐藏了美国国家劳动关系委员会（NLRB）的敏感劳动数据。DOGE由白宫顾问、亿万富翁马斯克领导，其任务是审查机构数据以符合新政府政策。举报人称，DOGE工程师访问NLRB内部系统后，数据流出异常增加，可能涉及工会和法律案件的敏感信息。DOGE成员还要求不记录其活动，并试图掩盖痕迹，关闭监控工具并手动删除访问记录。NLRB的IT部门已开始审查这一潜在的安全 breach，举报人担心数据可能被滥用，影响NLRB的独立性和公平性。举报人受到威胁，其指控得到了多方 corroboration。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对DOGE团队行为的合法性、道德性及其潜在影响的讨论

不同观点：
• [acdha] 认为DOGE团队的行为（如关闭监控工具、手动删除访问记录）与犯罪或国家支持的黑客行为相似，这非常令人震惊。同时提到可能存在技术上的失误导致暴露风险。
• [consumer451] 对网站内容审核标准表示不满，指出与技术和商业无关的外国政治新闻未被标记，而涉及美国技术和商业的故事却被标记，认为这种现象令人发笑。

43691142.article_content:
Whistleblower details how DOGE may have taken sensitive NLRB data
A whistleblower tells Congress and NPR that DOGE may have taken sensitive labor data and hid its tracks. "None of that ... information should ever leave the agency," said a former NLRB official.
Technology
A whistleblower's disclosure details how DOGE may have taken sensitive labor data
April 15, 2025
5:00 AM ET
Jenna McLaughlin
The DOGE team may have taken data related to union organizing and labor complaints and hid its tracks, according to a whistleblower.
Charlotte Gomez for NPR
hide caption
toggle caption
Charlotte Gomez for NPR
In the first days of March, a team of advisers from President Trump's new Department of Government Efficiency initiative arrived at the Southeast Washington, D.C., headquarters of the National Labor Relations Board.
The small, independent federal agency investigates and adjudicates complaints about unfair labor practices. It stores reams of potentially sensitive data, from confidential information about employees who want to form unions to proprietary business information.
The DOGE employees, who are effectively led by White House adviser and billionaire tech CEO Elon Musk, appeared to have their sights set on accessing the NLRB's internal systems. They've said their unit's overall mission is to review agency data for compliance with the new administration's policies and to cut costs and maximize efficiency.
Sponsor Message
But according to an official whistleblower disclosure shared with Congress and other federal overseers that was obtained by NPR, subsequent interviews with the whistleblower and records of internal communications, technical staff members were alarmed about what DOGE engineers did when they were granted access, particularly when those staffers noticed a spike in data leaving the agency. It's possible that the data included sensitive information on unions, ongoing legal cases and corporate secrets — data that four labor law experts tell NPR should almost never leave the NLRB and that has nothing to do with making the government more efficient or cutting spending.
Politics
DOGE says it needs to know the government's most sensitive data, but can't say why
Meanwhile, according to the disclosure and records of internal communications, members of the DOGE team asked that their activities not be logged on the system and then appeared to try to cover their tracks behind them, turning off monitoring tools and manually deleting records of their access — evasive behavior that several cybersecurity experts interviewed by NPR compared to what criminal or state-sponsored hackers might do.
White House senior adviser Elon Musk walks to the White House after landing in Marine One with President Trump on March 9.
Samuel Corum/Getty Images
hide caption
toggle caption
Samuel Corum/Getty Images
The employees grew concerned that the NLRB's confidential data could be exposed, particularly after they started detecting suspicious log-in attempts from an IP address in Russia, according to the disclosure. Eventually, the disclosure continued, the IT department launched a formal review of what it deemed a serious, ongoing security breach or potentially illegal removal of personally identifiable information. The whistleblower believes that the suspicious activity warrants further investigation by agencies with more resources, like the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency or the FBI.
Sponsor Message
The labor law experts interviewed by NPR fear that if the data gets out, it could be abused, including by private companies with cases before the agency that might get insights into damaging testimony, union leadership, legal strategies and internal data on competitors — Musk's SpaceX among them. It could also intimidate whistleblowers who might speak up about unfair labor practices, and it could sow distrust in the NLRB's independence, they said.
Technology
5 takeaways about NPR's reporting on the whistleblower report about DOGE at the NLRB
The new revelations about DOGE's activities at the labor agency come from a whistleblower in the IT department of the NLRB, who disclosed his concerns to Congress and the U.S. Office of Special Counsel in a detailed report that was then provided to NPR. Meanwhile, his attempts to raise concerns internally within the NLRB preceded someone "physically taping a threatening note" to his door that included sensitive personal information and overhead photos of him walking his dog that appeared to be taken with a drone, according to a cover letter attached to his disclosure filed by his attorney, Andrew Bakaj of the nonprofit Whistleblower Aid.
The whistleblower's account is corroborated by internal documentation and was reviewed by 11 technical experts across other government agencies and the private sector. In total, NPR spoke to over 30 sources across the government, the private sector, the labor movement, cybersecurity and law enforcement who spoke to their own concerns about how DO

data.title: 45-year mystery behind eerie photo from The Shining is believed to be solved
data.author: colinprince
data.article_summary: The 45-year mystery behind the eerie photo from *The Shining* may finally be solved. The photo, featured in Stanley Kubrick's 1980 horror film, appears to show the character Jack Torrance (played by Jack Nicholson) in a 1920s crowd. However, Nicholson's face was superimposed over the original subject. Retired academic Alasdair Spark and journalist Arik Tolar, after investigating, identified the man as Santos Casani (real name John Golman), a famous 1920s ballroom dancer from London. Casani's facial scars, caused by a plane crash during his time as a Royal Air Force (RAF) veteran, contributed to the unsettling appearance that sparked decades of speculation. The original photo was taken at the Royal Palace Hotel in Kensington, London, on February 14, 1921, during a ballroom dancing competition.

43660419.article_content:
45-year mystery behind eerie photo from The Shining is believed to be solved
Catherine Zhu | CBC Radio | Posted: April 10, 2025 10:50 PM | Last Updated: April 11
Man from infamous picture in the classic horror film identified by a retired academic and journalist
Image  |  Original getty photo
Caption: This is the original photograph that is claimed to have been superimposed on for The Shining's last scene. It shows patrons at a St. Valentine's dance and ballroom dancing competition in the Empress Rooms at the Royal Palace Hotel, Kensington, London, 14th February 1921. In the foreground, centre, with his arms open wide, is South African ballroom dancing teacher Santos Casani, a.k.a. John Golman.  (Morey/Topical Press Agency/Hulton Archive/Getty Images)
Load Image
Media Audio | As It Happens :  45-year mystery behind eerie photo from The Shining is believed to be solved
Open Full Embed in New Tab
(external link)
Loading external pages may require significantly more data usage than loading CBC Lite story pages.
It's a moment etched in horror movie history.
In Stanley Kubrick's 1980 horror classic
The
Shining,
the camera zooms in toward a black-and-white photograph hanging in the hallway of the Overlook Hotel. It's dated July 4, 1921. Dead centre stands Jack Torrance — played by Jack Nicholson — smiling in a crowd of partygoers.
But the photo wasn't taken on set with extras. It was a real photo from the 1920s, and Nicholson's face had been superimposed over someone. But whose face was it?
Now, after 45 years of theories and speculation, the mysterious man's identity and context of the eerie photo are believed to have been uncovered by an academic and journalist.
"I suppose I wouldn't have been so bothered if it hadn't been that the film mattered to me. I thought it was an important film," retired British academic Alasdair Spark told
As It Happens
host Nil Köksal.
The Shining
— based on the novel by Stephen King — tells the story of Jack and Wendy Torrance and their young son Danny, who spend a winter as caretakers of the haunted Overlook Hotel. Torrance, a recovering alcoholic and aspiring writer, slowly descends into madness as the hotel's supernatural forces take over him.
Conspiracy theories about the image's origins have circulated since the film's release.
Is 'The Shining' a secretly Canadian story? Homegrown writers reflect on its 40th anniversary
According to retired academic Alasdair Spark, a cropped version of the original photo — the one in which Jack Nicholson's face was superimposed — was revealed in a 1985 book,
The Complete Airbrush and Photo-Retouching Manual
, shedding new light on the mystery by revealing the man whose face had been covered up.
In 2012, the image resurfaced online, sparking fresh debates.
"[There were] lots of discussion about who he is and how strange he looks," said Spark.
Image  |  1985 book
Caption: According to retired academic Alasdair Spark, a cropped version of the original photo — the one in which Jack Nicholson’s face was superimposed — was revealed in a 1985 book, The Complete Airbrush and Photo-Retouching Manual, shedding new light on the mystery by revealing the man whose face had been covered up. (Submitted by Alasdair Spark)
Load Image
"Others said he was Edmund Platt, governor of the Federal Reserve in 1921, and the people around him were bankers, so the photo was proof that Kubrick secretly wanted to expose the financial elite," he recalled.
"I thought, 'I don't really think that's true and I'm going to find out and determine what actually is going on in the photograph,' and I'm happy to say I think I did."
Man in the photo
In 2024, a Reddit user named Connor Plunkett used a facial recognition tool to try and identify the man at the front of the crowd. It returned a match: Santos Casani, a famous ballroom dancer in 1920s London.
That's when Arik Tolar, a New York Times journalist on the visual investigations team, reached out to Spark to help investigate. Spark says Tolar had been skeptical, and "actually discounted it and didn't think it was a proper identification."
But Spark wasn't so sure, and together, they began digging further.
They found and looked at many other photos of Casani and discovered that his real name was John Golman. It was discovered that Casani, his stage name, had been in an accident that caused facial injuries.
"The scars on his face matched the scars on the unknown man, a.k.a. Casani. Bingo," said Spark.
"Many people had seen this disfigurement as devilish — that word was used — or evil. What I learned was he was an RAF veteran. He had crashed his aircraft and been badly wounded. He'd had a lot of plastic surgery, and that accounted for the strange look of his face."
Image  |  Alasdair Spark
Caption: Alasdair Spark, a retired British academic, dedicated nearly a year to uncovering the origins of the infamous photo from The Shining. (Submitted by Alasdair Spark)

data.title: How to Win an Argument with a Toddler
data.author: herbertl
data.article_summary: 本文主要讨论了为何无法与幼儿（或类似行为的人）进行有效辩论。幼儿并不理解辩论的本质，他们参与的是一种寻求连接、噪音或地位提升的行为，而非真正的思想交流。真正的辩论应带来洞见和结论，而与固执己见或缺乏善意的人辩论往往无效。若我们无法在辩论中改变观点，可能说明这并非真正的辩论，或者我们与不合适的人讨论。试图改变他人观点虽有趣，但通过讨论改变自己的观点也是一种收获。作者建议，对于与身份认同相关的信念，争论往往不值得。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何在辩论或讨论中有效沟通并可能改变对方的观点

不同观点：
• [ccleve] 认为通过理解并验证对方的情感（如对待幼儿的方式），可以让对方更容易接受你的观点，即便对方是成人也适用。强调理解和共享目标的重要性。
• [somenameforme] 主张辩论的目的不是说服对方，而是交换观点和深化自我认知。观点的改变是长期生活经验的结果，而非单纯的辩论。
• [speak_plainly] 强调在辩论中应保持宽容，理解对方表达观点的困难，帮助对方澄清观点，同时希望对方也能如此对待自己。
• [MathMonkeyMan] 指出在辩论中质问对方是否曾改变过观点是一种不真诚的辩论策略，可能被视为指责对方不理性。
• [PathOfEclipse] 认为辩论不总是为了学习或洞察，有时是为了说服第三方观众。总统辩论就是一个例子，候选人不是为了学习，而是为了说服选民。

How to win an argument with a toddler
You can’t.
That’s because toddlers don’t understand what an argument is and aren’t interesting in having one.
Toddlers (which includes defensive bureaucrats, bullies, flat earthers, folks committed to a specific agenda and radio talk show hosts) may indicate that they’d like to have an
argument
, but they’re actually engaging in connection, noise, play acting or a chance to earn status. It can be fun to be in opposition, to harangue or even to use power to change someone’s position.
An argument, though, is an exchange of ideas that ought to surface insight and lead to a conclusion.
If you’re regularly having arguments with well-informed people of goodwill, you will probably ‘lose’ half of them–changing your mind based on what you’ve learned.
If you’re not changing your mind, it’s likely you’re not actually having an argument
(or you’re hanging out with the wrong people.) While it can be fun to change someone else’s position, it’s also a gift to learn enough to change ours.
The toddler puts on a show of having an argument, but they are holding a tantrum in reserve. If they ‘win’ the argument, no tantrum is needed. If they lose, they can tell themselves that they tried but the other person deserved the tantrum because they didn’t listen.
“Tell me about other strongly-held positions you’ve changed as the result of a discussion like this one…” is a direct way to start a conversation about the argument you’re proposing to have. “What sort of information would make it likely you could see this in a different way?”
It probably doesn’t pay to argue over things we have chosen to believe as part of our identity.

data.title: Hacking the Postgres wire protocol
data.author: levkk
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了如何通过操纵Postgres的网络协议来实现多数据库查询。PgDog是一个网络代理，能够解析Postgres的简单协议和扩展协议，理解SQL并确定查询是读取还是写入数据，以及是否包含分片键。为了处理查询，PgDog使用`pg_query`库将SQL解析为抽象语法树，以识别分片键。分片函数则直接从Postgres的声明性分区中提取，使用哈希函数来确定分片编号。对于UPDATE、DELETE和INSERT等操作，PgDog根据是否存在分片键来路由查询。复杂情况如`IN`和`!=`操作符也能处理，但对于范围查询如`<`则需要查询所有分片。通过使用Rust和Postgres的源代码，PgDog实现了高效的分片路由。
data.comments_summary:

• 查询路由和复杂查询条件处理的具体实现细节。

43693326.article_content:
Hacking the Postgres wire protocol
Apr 14th, 2025
Lev Kokotov
PgDog is a network proxy and it can see every byte sent between Postgres and the clients. It understands SQL and can infer where queries should go, without requiring changes to application code.
In this article, we discuss how we handle the Postgres wire protocol and manipulate it to serve queries to multiple databases at the same time.
Protocol basics
Postgres has two ways to send queries over the network:
Simple protocol
Extended protocol
The simple protocol is called like that on purpose: it’s very simple. It has just one message, called
Query
which contains everything the server needs to execute it:
'Q' | \x00\x00\x00& | SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = 25\0
Postgres messages have a standard format. Each message starts with a single ASCII letter (1 byte), identifying the message type. It’s followed by a 32-bit signed integer, indicating the length of the payload, in bytes, with 4 bytes added for itself. The payload is unique for each message.
To route a query, PgDog needs to understand two things:
Does the query read or write data?
Does it contain a sharding key, and if so, what is it’s value?
To make this work, we need some help. To answer the first question, we could, theoretically, just look at the first word, and if it’s a “SELECT”, assume read intent. While this would work in most cases, we’ll miss some obvious ones, like CTEs.
The tricky part is finding the sharding key. For this, we need to actually interpret the query using a tool that understands SQL syntax. That’s called a parser, and luckily the Rust ecosystem already has a great library, called
pg_query
. The parser produces an Abstract Syntax Tree, a data structure we can read to find what we need:
let
ast
=
pg_query
::
parse
(
"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = 25"
);
pg_query
is special. It doesn’t actually implement parsing SQL. It works by extracting C source code directly from Postgres and wraps it with a nice Rust interface. This allows PgDog to understand
all
queries that Postgres can.
PgDog is all about sharding Postgres. Once we locate the sharding key in a query, we have to figure out what to do with it. Let’s do a quick detour into Postgres partitions.
The sharding function
Picking the right sharding function is critical. It’s not something you can easily change later. One thing I learned from doing this at Instacart: pick a sharding function which is available in multiple places. Let me explain.
In the real world, whatever you build, won’t be the
only
way to ingest or read data to/from your system. Either you don’t want to touch production (yet) or you just need to move some things around ad-hoc, you want engineers to be able to pre-process data in advance and have multiple ways to talk to your system.
For this reason, PgDog doesn’t implement a custom sharding function. It’s using the hashing function used in Postgres declarative partitions:
CREATE
TABLE
users
(
id
BIGINT
,
email
VARCHAR
)
PARTITION
BY
HASH
(
id
);
If you know the number of shards, you can create the same number of data partitions and just COPY data into the table. If you’re using FOREIGN tables with
postgres_fdw
, you can interact with your sharded database directly.
To make this work in PgDog, we took a page from the
pg_query
playbook. We could have implemented the function ourselves, but it’s much better to just take the code from Postgres and wrap it with a Rust interface.
Rust makes this pretty easy. Using the
cc
(C/C++ compiler) library and by copy/pasting some code, we have a working FFI interface to
hashfn.c
straight out of the Postgres source code tree. All we need is the right data to pass in, and apply the modulo operation to get the shard number.
Extracting parameters
Our example has only one filter:
id = 25
. This is the simplest case, but it’s also the most common one. Getting this value from SQL, using
pg_query
, is straightforward. Once we have it, we can pass it to the sharding function and we have a shard number.
UPDATE and DELETE queries work the same way. They all have (an optional) WHERE-clause, and if it has a filter with our sharding key, we can handle it. If it doesn’t, the query is sent to all shards (more on that below).
More complex examples, like
IN (1, 2, 3)
or
id != 25
can be handled as well. For the former, we can hash all values and route the query to the matching shards. For the latter, we can do the opposite. Some cases of course won’t work, e.g.,
WHERE id < 25
. That’s too many values to hash and this query will hit all shards anyway.
INSERT statements are a bit more interesting and come in two variants:
INSERT
INTO
users
(
id
,
email
)
VALUES
(
25
,
'
[email protected]
'
);
INSERT
INTO
users
VALUES
(
25
,
'
[email protected]
'
);
The first one specifies the column order, so we can just extract the sharding key directly. The second doesn’t, so we have to fetch the schema from Postgres and infer the column order. This is slightly more involved, but still a solvable problem

data.title: 7k-year-old skeletons from the green Sahara reveal a mysterious human lineage
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 考古学家在利比亚西南部的一个岩石庇护所中发现了15具 skeletons，其中包括两具约7000年前自然木乃伊化的女性遗体。这些遗体属于生活在“绿色撒哈拉”时期的古代人类，当时撒哈拉沙漠并非今天的荒漠，而是绿意盎然，湖泊河流遍布。研究人员通过DNA分析发现，这些牧民属于一个此前未知的、基因独特的人群，与亚撒哈拉非洲、近东和史前欧洲人群没有显著的遗传交流。这表明，牧业文化通过文化交流而非大规模迁徙传播。该发现为了解人类祖先的复杂历史提供了重要线索，但仍需更多研究来全面理解这一人群。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：基因组分析与人类迁徙模式的复杂性

不同观点：
• [Fg2Hj5mK] 认为基因组分析不断改变我们对人类迁徙模式的理解，强调人类进化历史比传统的“走出非洲”模型更为复杂，史前北非存在多个共存和杂交的血统。
• [mannyv] 指出，人群长时间的隔离是不寻常的，通常人类群体是流动的和杂交的。长时间的隔离可能意味着存在物理障碍，但同时质疑，如果人口规模大，他们应该会扩散。

43663713.article_content:
Archaeologists found 15 skeletons in a rock shelter in southwest Libya, including two naturally mummified women who died roughly 7,000 years ago.
Archaeological Mission in the Sahara, Sapienza University of Rome
Between 5,000 and 14,000 years ago, the
Sahara Desert
looked nothing like it does today. It was lush and green, with lakes and rivers supporting a variety of animals—including humans.
But who were these ancient ancestors? And where do they fit on the human family tree?
Researchers think they finally have some answers to these questions. They’ve successfully analyzed the DNA of two naturally mummified livestock herders who died roughly 7,000 years ago in present-day Libya, which was part of what’s known as the “green Sahara.”
Their analyses revealed a previously unknown—and largely genetically distinct—population of ancient humans, according to a new paper published this month in the journal
Nature
.
The individuals who lived in the green Sahara showed “no significant genetic influence from sub-Saharan populations to the south or Near Eastern and prehistoric European groups to the north,” says study co-author Johannes Krause, a geneticist at Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology, to
Reuters
’ Will Dunham.
“This suggests they remained genetically isolated despite practicing animal husbandry—a cultural innovation that originated outside Africa," Krause adds.
That finding was unexpected, as researchers had long theorized the green Sahara was a human migration corridor between North Africa and sub-Saharan Africa. “It’s surprising,” says
Eugenia
D’Atanasio
, a geneticist at the Sapienza University of Rome who was not involved with the research, to
Science
’s Andrew Curry. “I would have expected more gene flow across the green Sahara.”
Instead, the findings suggest that pastoralism—a nomadic lifestyle that involves herding livestock—spread across the green Sahara through “cultural exchange rather than large-scale migration,” says study co-author
Nada Salem
, a researcher at the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology, in a
statement
.
In the early 2000s, researchers discovered the remains of 15 ancient humans in southwest Libya near the border with Algeria. They found the skeletons in a rock shelter named Takarkori, along with pottery shards and rock art.
Archaeologists suspect the individuals buried at the site survived by hunting, fishing and herding animals like goats and sheep. Two of the skeletons were exceptionally well-preserved, with their skin, ligaments and tissues still intact, reports
CNN
’s Katie Hunt. Researchers determined they belonged to a pair of women in their 40s who had died around 5,000 B.C.E.
At first, researchers were only able to recover the women’s mitochondrial DNA, which gets passed down from mothers. But, eventually, they were able to sequence the mummies’ full genomes, which gave them a more complete understanding of their ancestry.
Their analyses revealed the green Sahara individuals likely branched off from the ancestors of sub-Saharan Africans roughly 50,000 years ago. Then, somehow, they remained genetically isolated for tens of thousands of years—a revelation that still perplexes researchers.
These individuals were “almost like living fossils,” Krause tells
BBC Science Focus
’ Tom Howarth.
“If you’d told me these genomes were 40,000 years old, I would have believed it,” he adds.
Scientists say they need to conduct more research to fully understand the individuals who lived in the green Sahara. DNA from two women may not be representative of all the humans who lived in this vast region over thousands of years.
Still, the paper makes a “key contribution” to scientists’ growing understanding of human ancestry, writes
Mary Prendergast
, an anthropologist at Rice University who was not involved with the research, in an accompanying
commentary
.
“Research is just beginning to reveal Africa’s complex population history, uncovering lineages barely detectable in the genomes of present-day people,” she writes. “In this context, even small sample numbers can shape our understanding of the past.”

data.title: Chroma: Ubisoft's internal tool used to simulate color-blindness
data.author: gm678
data.article_summary: Chroma是由Ubisoft开发的一站式解决方案，旨在检测游戏中的色盲相关问题。它能够模拟三种主要色盲类型： protanopia（红色盲）、deuteranopia（绿色盲）和tritanopia（蓝黄色盲），并在游戏屏幕上实时显示这些滤镜效果，帮助发现无障碍设计中的问题。该工具独立于任何特定游戏或引擎，适用于所有游戏，支持单显示器色彩模拟，最高可实时模拟60帧的游戏画面。其主要功能包括高精度结果、易于截图记录错误、可配置的用户界面等。开发过程中如遇CMake错误，可通过安装Microsoft.Windows.CppWinRT NuGet包解决。Chroma基于Apache-2.0许可证发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：颜色盲模拟工具及其在不同场景中的应用和实现

不同观点：
• [username256] 认为 Chroma 项目中的着色器代码似乎是直接复制自一个旧仓库，并没有在任何地方引用或提及原仓库。
• [maxnoe] 提到一个不同的工具（monolensAnd），该工具是为检查图形而开发的，并且具有跨平台功能，不同于主要讨论的游戏场景。
• [sph] 对颜色盲模式下游戏中的颜色去除和减弱处理提出质疑，认为应该通过色调调整或增强来帮助颜色盲用户，而不是简单地去除颜色，将其类比为通过静音来帮助听力障碍者。
• [Pet_Ant] 分享了自己使用 Chromatic Vision Simulator 来检查桌游的颜色盲可访问性的经验，并对该工具表示满意。
• [Thaxll] 赞扬了 Ubisoft 在可访问性方面的前沿工作。
• [fidotron] 询问了颜色盲模拟工具如何融入工作流程的问题，特别是 QA 团队如何使用这些工具进行反馈，以及与网页或移动应用设计中的不同使用场景。
• [ano-ther] 寻求一种能够评估颜色盲类型的工具，以便更好地解释自己如何看待颜色。
• [w4rh4wk5] 提供了一个替代方案，建议使用一个特定的着色器进行后处理。
• [charcircuit] 认为当前实现过于复杂，建议通过制作 OBS 插件来重用已有的游戏捕获和后处理工作。

补充讨论：
• 对于颜色盲模拟工具的具体应用场景存在不同看法，包括游戏、图形检查和桌游等。
• 讨论中涉及了工具的实现复杂度和技术选择，比如通过 OBS 插件简化工作流程。
• 对颜色盲模式下颜色处理方式的合理性存在争议，焦点在于是否应通过去除颜色来模拟颜色盲体验。
• 用户分享了多个具体工具和资源链接，提供了实际解决方案和替代方案。
• 对开源项目管理方式的批评，指出在 GitHub 项目中不正确使用资源树的问题。

Chroma
Chroma
helps in simulating different types of color blindness occurring in society.
Main purpose of this is to simulate 3 major
Color Blindness
types
Protanopia
,
Deuteranopia
and
Tritanopia
for our different games and aid accessibility team in performing various complex testing.
Following are key features:
Color Simulation on single monitor. This solution works on top of game and can be maximized as per requirement.
Work on all games. No dependency on any specific game or engine.
High performance. Able to simulation live gameplay upto 60 FPS.
Accurate results.
Simulation of all type of color blind forms.
Only available solution which capture screen live gameplay screen and simulate.
Easy screenshot to log error.
Easy and configurable UI.
For more details look into userguide
here
.
Known Issue During CMake Process
If you encounter the following error while running CMake without Visual Studio 2022:
error C2039: 'wait_for': is not a member of 'winrt::impl'
This issue may occur due to an outdated
CPPWinRT
library. To resolve it, install the
Microsoft.Windows.CppWinRT
NuGet package using the following command:
nuget install Microsoft.Windows.CppWinRT
Alternatively, ensure that your development environment is using an updated version of
CPPWinRT
.
The best option to avoid this issue is to use Visual Studio 2022.

Chroma is a one-stop solution for detecting color blindness-related issues in games. It replicates Protanopia, Deuteranopia, and Tritanopia filters over the game screen, helping users flag accessibility concerns in real-time.

data.title: Rotatum of Light
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对光学涡旋和轨道角动量光束研究的评论与好奇

不同观点：
• **addled**: 分享了自己过去在本科项目中类似实验的经历，提到在2007年使用古老的穿孔卡片来检查光束位置，并对当前研究中使用空间光调制器（SLM）以及生成角动量随距离变化的光束表示赞赏。他还提到研究中的螺旋图案让他感到很酷。

• **throw310822**: 对光学涡旋中光子是否相互作用表示好奇，提出问题：光子是否会像其他粒子一样相互作用产生涡旋？这显示出对光学涡旋形成机制的基本理解存在疑问。

• **interroboink**: 没有对科学内容作出深入评论，而是幽默地引用了《星际迷航》风格的语言，调侃了研究中复杂的科学术语如“adiabatic deformation of topology”和“Gouy phase factor”。这显示了一种对科学讨论的轻松态度，并通过引用流行文化增添了趣味性。

补充讨论：
• **技术细节**: addled 提到了实验技术的历史演变，特别是从2007年的实验设备（穿孔卡片）到现代设备（空间光调制器）的变化，显示出光学实验技术的进步。

• **争议焦点**: throw310822 对光子是否相互作用产生涡旋的疑问引发了对光学涡旋形成机制的讨论。虽然其他评论没有直接回应，但这是一个值得进一步解释的科学问题。

• **轻松调侃**: interroboink 的评论展示了科学讨论中轻松的一面，通过流行文化引用让讨论更加生动有趣，尽管没有深入讨论技术细节。

总结来看，评论既包含了专业背景的分享和技术进步的讨论，也包含了对科学现象的疑问和轻松的调侃。

data.title: You cannot have our user's data
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary:
SourceHut近期部署了Anubis以防止大型语言模型（LLM）爬虫的侵扰。文章澄清了SourceHut对爬虫行为的立场，强调用户数据应受到保护。根据其服务条款和robots.txt文件，自动化工具仅可用于存档或开放研究，禁止用于招聘、盈利等目的。未来条款更新将更明确规定爬虫使用条件，包括遵守robots.txt、标识软件及运营者信息、不影响服务性能，且仅限于搜索引擎索引、开放研究和存档用途。robots.txt还明确禁止用于营销、SEO和训练机器学习模型。

文章进一步讨论了爬虫对系统管理员的长期困扰，特别是LLM爬虫对互联网数据的抓取及其引发的性能问题。尽管部分社区建议通过优化或与LLM公司合作解决问题，SourceHut认为这些公司无权擅自使用数据，并拒绝为此类公司提供定制解决方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：网站对浏览器版本的限制与用户选择自由之间的矛盾；针对大型语言模型（LLM）爬取代码的版权保护与开放性之间的争议。

不同观点：
• **浏览器版本限制**：
   - **反对浏览器限制**：RadiozRadioz认为，网站通过多线程验证用户浏览器版本的做法是在人为设置障碍，限制旧版浏览器访问网站。他们认为，网站应该根据功能需求测试浏览器，而不是根据用户代理或特定浏览器版本来做决定。用户有权选择自己使用的浏览器，网站不应强行干预。
   - **支持技术需求**：虽然评论中没有明确支持这一做法的声音，但可以推测，网站方可能认为现代浏览器的使用能够提升安全性或用户体验，因此有必要设置这样的门槛。

• **版权与LLM爬取**：
   - **反对第三方限制代码使用**：dale_glass认为，项目的代码是基于Apache许可发布的，任何人都有权使用，包括用于AI分析。他们不认同第三方平台（如SourceHut）擅自限制代码的使用方式，并认为AI对项目有积极作用，帮助新手入门，且增加项目的可见性。
   - **支持版权保护**：bee_rider提出一种创意性的许可方式，即通过在代码中添加特定条款，要求任何基于该代码训练的AI模型必须开放源代码并免费使用。这种方式试图在法律框架内解决代码被用于训练AI但无法控制其分发的问题。

补充讨论：

• **技术替代方案**：
   - **替代验证机制**：RadiozRadioz建议使用贡献微小算力代替燃烧能量的多线程验证方式，比如通过微小的哈希计算为网站所有者提供一些经济收益。
   
• **对CloudFlare的批评**：
   - **CloudFlare的定性争议**：sltr提出对CloudFlare被称为“racketeer”的公平性进行讨论，但没有详细展开。这表明在社区中，CloudFlare的角色可能存在争议。

争议焦点：
• 浏览器版本限制是否合理，用户选择自由是否应被尊重。
• 如何在保护代码版权的同时，促进代码的开放使用和AI技术的发展。

43692998.article_content:
As you may have noticed, SourceHut has deployed
Anubis
to parts of our
services to protect ourselves from aggressive LLM crawlers.
1
Much ink has been
spilled on the subject of the LLM problem elsewhere, and we needn’t revisit that
here. I do want to take this opportunity, however, to clarify how SourceHut
views this kind of scraper behavior more generally, and how we feel that the
data entrusted to us by our users ought to be used.
Up until this point, we have offered some quiet assurances to this effect in a
few places, notably our terms of service and robots.txt file. Quoting the
former:
You may use automated tools to obtain public information from the services for
the purposes of archival or open-access research. You may not use this data
for recruiting, solicitation, or profit.
This has been part of our terms of service since they were originally written in
2018. With the benefit of hindsight, I might propose a different wording to
better reflect our intentions – but we try not to update the terms of service
too often because we have to send all users an email letting them know we’ve
done so. I have a proposed edit pending to include in the next batch of changes
to the terms which reads as follows:
You may use automated tools to access public SourceHut data in bulk (i.e.
crawlers, robots, spiders, etc) provided that:
Your software obeys the rules set forth in robots.txt
Your software uses a User-Agent header which clearly identifies your
software and its operators, including your contact information
Your software requests data at a rate which does not negatively affect the
performance of our services for other users
You may
only
collect this data for one or more of the following purposes:
Search engine indexing
Open-access research
Archival
You may not use automated tools to collect SourceHut data for solicitation,
profit, training machine learning models, or any other purpose not enumerated
here without explicit permission from SourceHut staff.
This text, or something similar, will be included in our next update to the
terms of service, which will probably ship around the time we finish setting up
our new European billing system.
A careful observer can see our views on scrapers elaborated on in our
robots.txt
file as well. It begins as follows:
# Our policy
#
# Allowed:
# - Search engine indexers
# - Archival services (e.g. IA)
#
# Disallowed:
# - Marketing or SEO crawlers
# - Anything used to feed a machine learning model
# - Bots which are too agressive by default. This is subjective, if you annoy
#   our sysadmins you'll be blocked.
#
# If you do not respect robots.txt or you deliberately circumvent it we will
# block your subnets and leave a bag of flaming dog shit on your mother's front
# porch.
One can infer from the tone of the last sentence that attempting to enforce
robots.txt is a frustrating, thankless task for our sysadmins.
To add to these resources, I’d like to elaborate a bit more on our views on
scrapers for you today. Scrapers have been a thorn in the side of sysadmins for
a very long time, but it’s particularly important as LLM scrapers seize the
entire Internet to feed into expensive, inefficient machine learning models –
ignoring the copyright (
or copyleft
, as it were) of the data as
they go. The serious costs and widespread performance issues and outages caused
by reckless scrapers has been on everyone’s mind in the sysadmin community as of
late, and has been the subject of much discussion online.
Aside from the much-appreciated responses of incredulity towards LLM operators,
and support and compassion for sysadmins from much of the community, a
significant minority views this problem as less important than we believe it to
be. Many of their arguments reduce to victim blaming – that it’s not that hard
to handle this volume of traffic, that we should be optimized to better deal
with it, that we need more caching or to improve our performance, or that we
should pay a racketeer like CloudFlare to make the problem go away. Some suggest
that sysadmins should be reaching out to LLM companies to offer them more
efficient ways to access our data to address the problem.
Of course, not all software is necessarily able to be as resource efficient as
Joe Naysayer’s static website. Moreover, LLM companies are not particularly
interested in the more expensive route of building software integrations for
each data source they scrape when they could go the cheap route of making us all
pay for the overhead; nor should us sysadmins have to spend the finite time and
resources at
our
disposal (often much more modest than the resources available
to these LLM companies) negotiating with terrorists and building bespoke
solutions for
them
.

assumption: that these companies are entitled to this data. This assumption has

data.title: WEIRD – a way to be on the web
data.author: weinzierl
data.article_summary: "Weird" 是一个新的网络平台，结合了 WordPress 的网站功能、Notion 的编辑体验和 Linktree 的简洁性，帮助用户在网络上创建个人空间。它允许用户在2分钟内创建网站，拥有自己的数字身份，并通过链接列表等简单方式表达自我。平台支持数字园艺，让用户轻松发布和管理内容，还计划推出与开放网络项目和联邦网络圈的连接功能。Weird 旨在构建一个小型、开放的网络生态，提供类似社交网络的功能，但更加注重用户隐私和数据自主权。平台还提供自动化发布策略和与其他独立网络服务的互通性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“Weird”项目的评价与讨论，涉及可访问性、术语使用、项目独特性及其技术实现等方面。

不同观点：
• **可访问性问题**：用户dimal指出，网站上的动画横幅文本对像他们这样的神经多样性（neurodivergent）人群造成了困扰，因为无休止的动画使他们难以集中注意力阅读内容。这涉及到网页开发中的无障碍设计问题，尤其是对某些人群的排斥。

• **术语使用争议**：seafoamteal认为使用“agentic development”这一术语有风险，因为这可能让一些用户联想到LLM（大型语言模型）等不受欢迎的技术，从而影响他们对项目的初始印象。

• **项目需求质疑**：settsu对项目的定位和目标用户表示怀疑，认为其描述可能过于复杂，不清楚有多少人真正需要这种产品。

• **项目支持与期待**：duncancarroll对项目表示支持，认为它满足了明显的需求，并且自己很期待尝试使用。

• **项目背景与未来发展**：erlend_sh作为项目联合创始人之一，介绍了Weird的背景和发展方向，并将其与Roomy项目联系起来。

• **技术实现与开放网络的讨论**：rambambram分享了自己对RSS和OPML技术组合的看法，认为Weird的“federated webring”功能具有潜力，并讨论了开放网络的真正精神。

• **项目独特性质疑**：imaginationra认为Weird与Web 2.0的模板化网站类似，缺乏独特性，并提到mmm.page作为更具创造性的替代方案。

• **项目名称与技术趋势**：psoots指出，“agentic”这一术语在AI代理兴起的背景下可能引发混淆，建议谨慎使用。

• **技术问题反馈**：dudefeliciano在尝试创建个人资料时遇到500错误，指出了项目在技术实现上的具体问题。

• **个人偏好与语言风格**：Yie1cho表示，看到“interwebs”一词便会停止阅读，反映了用户在语言风格上的个人偏好。

• **对“正式化”和早期网络精神的讨论**：superkuh认为Weird过于正式，缺乏早期网络的独特性，并强调保持HTTP/1.1和HTTP+HTTPS对于维持网站长久生命力的重要性。

补充讨论：
• 项目名称和术语使用的争议反映了用户对新技术和趋势的敏感性及其潜在影响。
• 可访问性问题提醒开发者在设计和开发过程中需要考虑更广泛的用户群体，尤其是神经多样性人群的需求。
• 技术实现和早期网络精神的讨论涉及对开放网络及其技术基础的更深层次思考。

43691891.article_content:
Weird
a way to be on the web!
Cultivate your personal space on the interwebs
from scribble-saplings to digital garden, in communion with fellow
weirdos.
Weird is a brand new thing, but: Think of it as if
WordPress
and
Notion
had a Linktree-shaped baby. That is to say, a WordPress-type website engine
with the editing experience of Notion and the simplicity of
Linktree
.
Say hello, again, to the weird web
Village-scale software 🏘️
Like itch.io, but for any Open Web project
Like a distributed Wikipedia for projects
Like the internet archive for - you guessed it - projects 💫
A social network for your thoughts
An ecosystem for living ideas 🌱
Essentials
Digital homeownership:
Every profile on Weird-net is also a website
; use our (sub)domain or bring your own.
2-minute site creation:
Escape the
content-creation imperative
by grabbing whatever self-links you’ve got and re-consolidate your digital identity.
Reclaim your captured content:
Automated pipelines for
PESOS & POSSE posting strategies
. Write (or at least post) like
Molly White
and
Cory Doctorow
!
Grow web gardens:
Forget about chronological web logs, we're doing
digital gardening
now. Casually plop your tiny blurb-seeds down and cultivate them at your leisure.
Enter the indieverse:
Connect to the
WWWapps Directory weird#283
, outside the dreary confines of big tech. 🚧Coming soon
Find the others:
Participate in the
chatty community gardens
of
federated webrings
. 🚧Coming soon
just like milk and honey...
Weird is a combination of two things that go together
➢
Magic Website Creator
To fully inhabit the World Wide Web you need to create your digital self within it.
For a lot of us, the “simple” prospect of filling in that web page with content presents an insurmountable
writer’s block
.
That’s why we start with
link lists
as a primitive building block. Make a
list
of 1, 3 or however many
links
that say something, anything, about you.
Whatever you’ve listed, you’ve done it! You told us something about your self, and with that you are taking up a bit of space on the web, as you should.
➣
Web Passports
Weird is the “Google-login” button of the alt-web. A
web of the people
, powered by people's websites instead of those pesky totalitarian mega-platforms.
By making - or merely connecting - your website with Weird you will soon be able to access and interact with the small, open and indie web just as easily as the regular web works today. Same conveniences, without the dark patterns, spying and data theft.
Say hello, again, to the weird web
Village-scale software 🏘️
Like itch.io, but for any Open Web project
Like a distributed Wikipedia for projects
Like the internet archive for - you guessed it - projects 💫
A social network for your thoughts
An ecosystem for living ideas 🌱
Intro to Project Weird
'Agentic Developers' are the infrastructure-minded partners of '
Barefoot Developers
'.
Agentic development
is happening when we build products based on the combined principles of local-first and peer-to-peer, maximizing for user agency by way of user-centric design.

data.title: Google Search to redirect its country level TLDs to Google.com
data.author: lapcat
data.article_summary: Google将开始将其国家代码顶级域名（ccTLD）如google.fr、google.ng等重定向到google.com。这是因为Google搜索在提供本地化体验方面有了改进，所有用户无论使用哪个域名都能获得相同的本地搜索结果。此次变更将逐步在未来几个月内推行，大部分用户不会感受到明显变化，但可能需要重新登录或调整搜索设置。此举不会影响搜索功能或谷歌在各国法律下的义务，但可能会对引流和登录体验产生轻微影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google 更改域名结构（如从 maps.google.com 到 www.google.com/maps）的原因及其技术影响

不同观点：
• [snowwrestler] 认为，Google 更改域名结构可能是为了利用第一方 cookie 的安全模型，通过在同一根域名下的单一子域运行所有服务，能够更好地整合数据，从而提升数据收集的效率。

• [phillipseamore] 持不同看法，认为以往的模式（通过 ccTLD 重定向）会消耗大量资源和带宽，包括进行 GeoIP 查找、cookie 检查以及重复的请求重定向。他认为，新的更改应会减少用户延迟（无需重定向、额外的DNS查找和TLS握手），并增强资源缓存效率。

• [jsheard] 提出一个问题，Google 已经拥有 .google 顶级域名（TLD），理论上是否可以使用 https://google 这种形式，并质疑是否存在相关规则限制。

• 关于 Google 是否能使用 https://google 的问题引发了一些技术规则上的讨论。

Google Search to redirect its country level TLDs to Google.com
Google will gradually roll out this change over the coming months.

Google will begin redirecting its country code top-level domain names (ccTLD) versions of its Google domain to Google.com. That means if you frequent google.fr (in France), google.ng (in Nigeria) and so on, you will be redirected to Google.com.
Why the change.
Google
said
, “Over the years, our ability to provide a local experience has improved.
In 2017,
we began providing the same experience with local results for everyone using Search, whether they were using
google.com
or their country’s ccTLD.” “Because of this improvement, country-level domains are no longer necessary,” Google added.
Google said, “we’ll begin redirecting traffic from these ccTLDs to
google.com
to streamline people’s experience on Search.”
The impact.
For the most part, most searchers should not notice any difference. When you are redirected, there is a chance you may have to login to Google again and also reconfigure some of your search settings.
But overall, there won’t be any significant changes. Google wrote, “It’s important to note that while this update will change what people see in their browser address bar, it won’t affect the way Search works, nor will it change how we handle obligations under national laws.”
Timing.
This change will begin today but “will be rolled out gradually over the coming months,” the company said.
Why we care.
You may notice slightly different referral traffic from Google Search, related to this change.
This may also impact your signed in experience with Google.com in the short term.
But outside of that, there should be no other large changes with these ccTLD changes for Google Search.

data.title: LightlyTrain: Better Vision Models, Faster – No Labels Needed
data.author: michal-l
data.article_summary: LightlyTrain是一个PyTorch框架，旨在通过自监督预训练帮助计算机视觉模型在无标签数据上进行预训练，从而减少标注成本并加速模型部署。它适用于各种领域，如视频分析、农业、汽车、医疗和零售等，支持多种模型架构和任务（如检测、分类、分割）。该工具无需自我监督学习专业知识，支持单GPU、多GPU及多节点设置，并兼容Torchvision、TIMM、YOLO等多种模型库。用户可以通过简单的命令行或Python接口使用，并将预训练模型导出用于微调或推理。LightlyTrain还支持TensorBoard和Weights & Biases等工具来监控训练进度。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LightlyTrain工具在计算机视觉自监督学习中的应用及其优势

不同观点：
• [joelio182] 认为LightlyTrain在处理领域偏移问题上具有重要意义，特别是在标签有限的情况下，可以直接在无标签数据上进行预训练。他还对该工具在更小众领域（如卫星或工业检测数据）中的表现表示好奇，并称赞其开源。
• [liopeer] 简短地表达了对LightlyTrain作为大众化计算机视觉预训练框架的兴奋之情。
• [leonax97] 强调了LightlyTrain作为一个生产就绪的预训练框架的价值。
• [isusmelj] 作为Lightly AI的联合创始人，详细介绍了LightlyTrain的功能和优势，包括无需标签、性能提升、领域适应、支持流行模型、易用性和可扩展性等。他还提供了基准测试结果和相关链接，并表示愿意讨论技术、基准或使用案例，同时提到商业许可证的可获得性。

补充讨论：
• LightlyTrain的主要功能和特点被详细介绍，包括其在无标签数据上进行预训练的能力，以及在特定领域（如医疗、农业、自动驾驶）中显著提升性能的潜力。
• 提供了具体的基准测试结果，例如在COCO数据集上，使用LightlyTrain预训练的YOLOv8-s模型在仅使用10%标签的情况下，mAP提升了+14%（相比ImageNet权重）和+34%（相比无预训练）。
• 讨论了该工具的开源许可证（AGPL-3.0）以及商业许可证的可获得性，以满足不同用户的需求。

Train Better Models, Faster - No Labels Needed
LightlyTrain brings self-supervised pretraining to real-world computer vision pipelines, using
your unlabeled data to reduce labeling costs and speed up model deployment. Leveraging the
state-of-the-art from research, it pretrains your model on your unlabeled, domain-specific
data, significantly reducing the amount of labeling needed to reach a high model performance.
This allows you to focus on new features and domains instead of managing your labeling cycles.
LightlyTrain is designed for simple integration into existing training pipelines and supports
a wide range of model architectures and use-cases out of the box.
Why LightlyTrain
💸
No Labels Required
: Speed up development by pretraining models on your unlabeled image and video data.
🔄
Domain Adaptation
: Improve models by pretraining on your domain-specific data (e.g. video analytics, agriculture, automotive, healthcare, manufacturing, retail, and more).
🏗️
Model & Task Agnostic
: Compatible with any architecture and task, including detection, classification, and segmentation.
🚀
Industrial-Scale Support
: LightlyTrain scales from thousands to millions of images. Supports on-prem, cloud, single, and multi-GPU setups.
On COCO, YOLOv8-s models pretrained with LightlyTrain achieve high performance across all tested label fractions.
These improvements hold for other architectures like YOLOv11, RT-DETR, and Faster R-CNN.

announcement post
for more details.

data.title: JEP 506: Scoped Values final for Java 25
data.author: ludovicianul
data.article_summary: JEP 506 提出引入 "scoped values" 机制，允许方法在线程内及其子线程中共享不可变数据。相比线程局部变量（ThreadLocal），scoped values 更易于理解和推理，具有更低的空间和时间成本，尤其在与虚拟线程（JEP 444）和结构化并发（JEP 505）结合使用时。该机制经历了多个预览和改进阶段（JEP 429, JEP 446, JEP 464, JEP 481, JEP 487），并计划在 JDK 25 中正式引入。其目标包括易用性、可理解性、健壮性和高效性，但不旨在改变 Java 语言或废弃 ThreadLocal API。Scoped values 解决了在方法间传递共享数据时的繁琐问题，尤其在大型程序中不同组件间传递上下文时非常实用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Java中通过隐式参数传递上下文的机制及其与现有机制的比较

不同观点：
• [bhawks] 认为隐式参数传递（如参数走私）过于“魔法化”，不如Golang中的context.Context那样明确和广泛接受。虽然他承认在Java生态中引入类似Golang的机制可能不现实，但从实际角度看，这种隐式传递可能是传播上下文的唯一可靠方法。

• [Pet_Ant] 认为ScopedValue机制类似于一种DSL，用于替代ThreadLocal，并且能更好地表示变量的生命周期，而不是像ThreadLocal那样作为全局变量。他提到虚拟线程的引入会大幅增加线程数量，传统的ThreadLocal机制难以应对。虽然他承认这种机制在处理大量数据时可能有好处，但对于大多数企业级CRUD应用来说，可能并不适用。他还猜测这种机制可能与函数式编程中的Monad概念有关，但表示自己不是函数式编程的专家。

• [skerit] 对ScopedValue提案表示感兴趣，认为自己在某些情况下可能会使用这种机制。

• [djenndhxhd] 提到 tramp parameters（传递参数）是常见现象，若不谨慎处理会带来问题。他认可ScopedValue提案的价值。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于隐式参数传递是否过于“魔法化”以及其在Java生态中的适用性。
• ScopedValue相对于ThreadLocal的优势和适用场景，特别是在处理大量虚拟线程时的表现。
• 对ScopedValue机制是否属于Monad的猜测，反映了参与者对函数式编程概念的不同理解。
• 对ScopedValue提案的实际应用价值存在一定共识，多数参与者认为在特定场景下可能有帮助。
