Summary
Introduce
scoped values
, which enable a method to share immutable data both with its callees within a thread, and with child threads. Scoped values are easier to reason about than thread-local variables. They also have lower space and time costs, especially when used together with virtual threads (
JEP 444
) and structured concurrency (
JEP 505
).
History
The scoped values API was proposed for incubation by
JEP 429
(JDK 20), proposed for preview by
JEP 446
(JDK 21), and subsequently improved and refined by
JEP 464
(JDK 22),
JEP 481
(JDK 23), and
JEP 487
(JDK 24).
We here propose to finalize the scoped values API in JDK 25, without further change.
Goals
Ease of use
— It should be easy to reason about dataflow.
Comprehensibility
— The lifetime of shared data should be apparent from the syntactic structure of code.
Robustness
— Data shared by a caller should be retrievable only by legitimate callees.
Performance
— Data should be efficiently sharable across a large number of threads.
Non-Goals
It is not a goal to change the Java programming language.
It is not a goal to require migration away from thread-local variables, or to deprecate the existing
ThreadLocal
API.
Motivation
Java applications and libraries are structured as collections of classes which contain methods. These methods communicate through method calls.
Most methods allow a caller to pass data to a method by passing the data as parameters. When method
A
wants method
B
to do some work for it, it invokes
B
with the appropriate parameters, and
B
may pass some of those parameters to
C
, and so forth.
B
may have to include in its parameter list not only the things
B
directly needs but also the things
B
has to pass to
C
. For example, if
B
is going to set up and execute a database call, it might want a Connection passed in, even if
B
is not going to use the Connection directly.
Most of the time this "pass what your indirect callees need" approach is the most effective and convenient way to share data. However, sometimes it is impractical to pass all the data that every indirect callee might need in the initial call.
An example
It is a common pattern in large Java programs to transfer control from one component (a "framework") to another ("application code") and then back. For example, a web framework could accept incoming HTTP requests and then call an application handler to handle it. The application handler may then call the framework to read data from the database or to call some other HTTP service.
@Override
public void handle(Request request, Response response) {
// user code, called by framework
...
var userInfo = readUserInfo();
...
}
private UserInfo readUserInfo() {
// call framework
return (UserInfo)framework.readKey("userInfo", context);
}
The framework may maintain a
FrameworkContext
object, containing the authenticated user ID, the transaction ID, etc., and associate it with the current transaction. All framework operations use the
FrameworkContext
object, but it's unused by (and irrelevant to) user code.
In effect, the framework must be able to communicate its internal context from its
serve
method (which calls the user's
handle
method) to its
readKey
method:
4. Framework.readKey <--------+ use context
3. Application.readUserInfo   |
2. Application.handle         |
1. Framework.serve  ----------+ create context
The simplest way to do this is by passing the object as an argument to all methods in the call chain:
@Override
void handle(Request request, Response response, FrameworkContext context) {
...
var userInfo = readUserInfo(context);
...
}
private UserInfo readUserInfo(FrameworkContext context) {
return (UserInfo)framework.readKey("userInfo", context);
}
There is no way for the user code to assist in the proper handling of the context object. At worst, it could interfere by mixing up contexts; at best it is burdened with the need to add another parameter to all methods that may end up calling back into the framework. If the need to pass a context emerges during redesign of the framework, adding it requires not only the immediate clients — those user methods that directly call framework methods or those that are directly called by it — to change their signature, but all intermediate methods as well, even though the context is an internal implementation detail of the framework and user code should not interact with it.

Developers have traditionally used
thread-local variables
, introduced in Java 1.2, to help share data between methods on the call stack without resorting to method parameters. A thread-local variable is a variable of type

43691268.article_summary: JEP 506 提出引入 "scoped values" 机制，允许方法在线程内及其子线程中共享不可变数据。相比线程局部变量（ThreadLocal），scoped values 更易于理解和推理，具有更低的空间和时间成本，尤其在与虚拟线程（JEP 444）和结构化并发（JEP 505）结合使用时。该机制经历了多个预览和改进阶段（JEP 429, JEP 446, JEP 464, JEP 481, JEP 487），并计划在 JDK 25 中正式引入。其目标包括易用性、可理解性、健壮性和高效性，但不旨在改变 Java 语言或废弃 ThreadLocal API。Scoped values 解决了在方法间传递共享数据时的繁琐问题，尤其在大型程序中不同组件间传递上下文时非常实用。

data.title: CT scans could cause 5% of cancers, study finds; experts note uncertainty
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 一篇发表于《JAMA Internal Medicine》的新研究估计，2023年美国进行的9300万次CT扫描可能导致未来出现10.3万例癌症，约占每年确诊癌症的5%。这些癌症多为肺癌和结肠癌，与腹部及盆腔CT扫描关系最大。尽管CT扫描能拯救生命，但其带来的辐射暴露可能增加癌症风险，风险程度与饮酒和肥胖相似。专家强调，应谨慎使用CT扫描，优化剂量，并在有替代选项时让患者参与决策。尽管CT扫描增加的癌症风险较小（约0.1%），但其使用量巨大，医生应权衡利弊，避免不必要的检查。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：CT扫描的利弊权衡，包括其对健康的潜在风险与诊断效益之间的争议。

不同观点：
• **TaupeRanger**：认为该模型存在问题，未明确患者是否是独特的个体，也未提及患者数据如何处理，尤其质疑模型能否回答患者关心的核心问题，即扫描对寿命和生活质量的影响。
• **delichon**：基于个人经历，质疑CT扫描的必要性，指出某些诊断结果本可以通过无创方式获得，却选择了有辐射的CT扫描。
• **kristjansson**：引用Scott Alexander的文章，指出CT扫描具有较高的风险（如1/650的死亡风险），并认为这种风险是不可忽视的。
• **daedrdev**：指出广泛筛查罕见疾病的弊端，包括误诊和过度治疗的风险，认为筛查的危害可能超过疾病本身的危害，特别是在疾病较为罕见的情况下。
• **Tepix**：提出核心问题，即CT扫描拯救的生命数量与因其引发癌症而失去的生命数量的比较。
• **sebastian_z**：强调不同CT扫描仪的辐射剂量差异，建议患者可以选择低剂量扫描仪以减少辐射风险。
• **enjoytheview**：计算个人 lifetime risk（终生风险）的小幅增加，但认为保持健康生活方式（如不吸烟、不喝酒）更为实际的降低风险方式。
• **lokar**：批评媒体对统计数据的呈现方式，认为应关注个体风险而非群体数据，并指出预防其他癌症可能影响CT扫描的相对风险。
• **jchw**：表达个人对健康焦虑的感受，虽然承认个体层面的担忧无必要，但仍对CT扫描的辐射量感到不安。
• **drpgq**：提出通过比较美国和加拿大人群的CT扫描频率和健康结果来验证CT扫描影响的可能性。
• **tgv**：质疑是否可以通过研究其他CT扫描（如骨折扫描）来验证其致癌风险，因为这些部位癌症罕见。
• **sakex**：询问MRI与CT的区别，表现出对两种诊断方式的不了解。
• **Zezima**：认为需要CT扫描的病情本身通常比CT可能引发的癌症风险更危险，主张继续使用CT。
• **sagolikasoppor**：基于个人多次CT扫描的经历，表达对辐射剂量的担忧，但也承认CT在诊断和治疗中的有效性。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于CT扫描的必要性及其对健康的潜在风险，尤其是在筛查和诊断罕见疾病时的权衡。
• 个体对辐射风险的态度存在差异，一些人更关注具体风险的量化数据，而另一些人则更在意如何通过其他方式降低整体健康风险。
• 不同CT扫描仪的辐射剂量差异被提及，表明患者在选择诊断方式时有一定的自主性。
• 有讨论试图通过不同方式验证CT扫描的致癌风险，如跨国比较或研究其他非癌症部位的扫描数据。

Computed tomography scans have become vital, even lifesaving, medical imaging for diagnosing and monitoring health conditions. But they do expose patients to ionizing radiation at levels linked to higher risks of cancer. In
a new study in JAMA Internal Medicine
, researchers tried to estimate what those higher risks are exactly—and although the estimates come with uncertainty, they may seem startling.
Based on data from 93 million CT scans performed on 62 million people in 2023, the researchers estimated that the CT scans would lead to 103,000 future cancers. To put that in context, those 103,000 cancers would account for about 5 percent of cancers diagnosed each year, based on the current cancer rates and the current usage of CT scans. And the estimate puts CT scans on par with alcohol consumption and obesity in terms of risk factors for developing cancer.
The most common types of cancers estimated to be a result of CT scans were lung cancer and colon cancer—two cancers that are becoming more common in younger people for reasons experts do not fully understand. The types of CT scans linked to the greatest number of cancers were abdomen and pelvis CT scans.
The study's authors—led by epidemiology and biostatistics researchers at the University of California, San Francisco—concluded that doctors should use CT scans when they can be justified and at optimized doses to balance the risks and benefits.
"CT is frequently lifesaving, yet its potential harms are often overlooked, and even very small cancer risks will lead to a significant number of future cancers given the tremendous volume of CT use in the United States," they write. Since 2007, use of CT scans has increased 35 percent, an increase not entirely explained by population growth, they note.
Outside experts agreed that CT scans should be used judiciously. But they highlighted that there is much uncertainty in the modeling, which tried to assess absorbed doses in different organs and the increased risk of site-specific cancer. While some large studies have found links between CT scans in children and young adults and increased risks of
blood
and
brain cancers
, the risks for adults have largely been extrapolated from studies on Japanese atomic bomb survivors or people with occupational radiation exposures.
Uncertainty and balancing
"The estimates, while based on the best models available to the authors, are indirect, so there is considerable uncertainty about the estimates," Stephen Duffy, emeritus professor of Cancer Screening at Queen Mary University of London, said in a statement. "Thus, I would say to patients that if you are recommended to have a CT scan, it would be wise to do so."
Duffy also highlighted that in the context of a person's overall risk of cancer, CT scans don't move the needle much. There were a little over 100,000 cancers linked to 93 million scans. "This amounts to around a 0.1 percent increase in cancer risk over the patient's lifetime per CT examination," he said. The lifetime risk of cancer in the US population is
around 40 percent
. Thus, the additional risk from CT scans "is small." Overall, when a CT scan is deemed necessary, the "likely benefit in diagnosis and subsequent treatment of disease outweighs the very small increase in cancer risk."
Doreen Lau, a cancer biology expert at Brunel University of London, agreed: "The findings don’t mean that people should avoid CT scans when recommended by a doctor. In most cases, the benefit of detecting or ruling out serious illness far outweighs the very small risk of harm."
Still, the rise in CT scans in recent years may suggest that doctors could cut back on their use. In
an accompanying editorial
, Ilana Richman of Yale University and Mitchell Katz of NYC Health and Hospitals discussed ways that doctors could make sure they're balancing risks and benefits before using CT scans, including using diagnostic algorithms and offering alternative imaging options, such as ultrasounds and magnetic resonance imaging (MRIs).
"As with all complex problems, there will be no simple solution," they write. But, "educating clinicians about avoiding low-value testing and, in circumstances where alternatives are readily available, involving patients in the decision to do a CT scan may help shift culture and practice."
Beth Mole
Senior Health Reporter
Beth Mole
Senior Health Reporter
Beth is Ars Technica’s Senior Health Reporter. Beth has a Ph.D. in microbiology from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and attended the Science Communication program at the University of California, Santa Cruz. She specializes in covering infectious diseases, public health, and microbes.

data.author: mdp2021
data.article_summary: 哲学专业学生Mohsen Mahdawi在申请美国公民身份面试时，被ICE执法人员戴着头套和面具带走，目前去向不明。他的律师称，此次拘捕是特朗普政府对他支持巴勒斯坦行为的报复，且违反宪法。Mahdawi是绿卡持有者，出生于约旦河西岸的难民营，2014年移居美国。他曾接受《60分钟》采访，强调反对反犹主义与支持巴勒斯坦自由斗争并行不悖。联邦法院已发布临时限制令，防止他被驱逐出境。

43693375.article_content:
Mohsen Mahdawi, a philosophy major at Columbia University who is due to graduate later this semester, was attending a US citizenship application interview in Vermont on Monday when Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents wearing hoods and masks took him from the building, put him into an unmarked car, and drove off.
His current whereabouts are “unknown”, said his lawyer, according to the
BBC
.
Mahdawi is a green card holder. According to the BBC:
His lawyer, Luna Droubi, said: “The Trump administration detained Mohsen Mahdawi in direct retaliation for his advocacy on behalf of Palestinians and because of his identity as a Palestinian.
“His detention is an attempt to silence those who speak out against the atrocities in Gaza. It is also unconstitutional.”
The attorney applied to a federal court for a temporary restraining order to prevent US immigration authorities moving Mr Mahdawi out of Vermont or expelling him from the US.
Judge William Sessions, an Obama appointee, quickly granted that order.
The court filing says Mr Mahdawi was born in a refugee camp in the West Bank and moved to the US in 2014.
It describes the philosophy major as a committed Buddhist who believes in “non-violence and empathy as a central tenet of his religion”.
Mahdawi was interviewed last year by
60 Minutes
about the student protests at Columbia regarding Israel’s response to Hamas’s attack on October 7th, 2023. In the interview he says:
To be anti-Semitic is unjust. And the fight for the freedom of Palestine and the fight against anti-Semitism go hand in hand, because injustice anywhere is a threat to justice everywhere.
A clip of the interview is below.
(via Shen-Yi Liao)

data.title: The last RadioShack in Maryland is closing
data.author: ivewonyoung
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于RadioShack等电子产品实体店的衰落及其影响

不同观点：
• **怀旧与情感价值**：
  - 一些用户（如delichon、WorldPeas、marcusb）怀念RadioShack，认为它曾经是获取电子元件和工具的重要场所，并对它的关闭感到遗憾。他们分享了个人经历，如购买电子计算器、PS2适配器和多用电表，强调了RadioShack在电子爱好者和DIY项目中的重要性。
  - 用户0xbadcafebee甚至提到了使用RadioShack的零件进行“黑客”活动的经历，表达了对过去探索和技术实验的怀念。

• **经济与竞争压力**：
  - 用户tombert指出，RadioShack在与大卖场和亚马逊等在线零售商竞争中逐渐失利，尽管理解这种趋势，但对其消亡感到惋惜。
  - 用户beloch分享了加拿大RadioShack转型为“The Source”并最终关闭的平行历史，强调了品牌重塑和价格问题对其衰落的影响。

• **实体店的现状与未来**：
  - 用户evanmoran描述了带孩子去GameStop卖旧游戏机的经历，强调了实体店带来的独特体验和社区互动，尽管其经济模式不可持续。
  - 用户codingdave提到，虽然RadioShack品牌已经衰落，但仍有少数独立运营的RadioShack店存在。

• **个人经历与职业体验**：
  - 用户colecut分享了在RadioShack短暂工作的经历，描述了其在2009年的状态，包括推销电池和手机计划的压力，表达了对零售工作的不适应。
  - 用户karpatic回忆了在RadioShack工作时与其他顾客交流技术和爱好的经历，强调了社交互动的价值。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：
  - 一些用户（如bityard、magnusss）提到了在RadioShack购物时的价格问题，尽管其提供的元件最终有用，但价格并不总是最具竞争力的。
  - bityard还讨论了亚马逊和AliExpress在电子元件采购中的局限性，表达了对电子爱好因经济和关税问题而逐渐消失的担忧。

• **其他值得注意的讨论点**：
  - 用户reverendsteveii以幽默方式提到，将“The Last RadioShack In Maryland”视为自己最喜欢的Tom Waits歌曲，增加了讨论的文化层次。
  - panzagl提到RadioShack品牌的组件在Hobbytowns等其他商店中的存在，反映了其影响力的扩散和最终消失。

总体而言，讨论围绕RadioShack的消亡及其在电子爱好者和社区中的重要性展开，涉及怀旧、经济竞争、个人经历和未来展望等多方面内容。

data.title: Generate videos in Gemini and Whisk with Veo 2
data.author: meetpateltech
data.article_summary: 自2025年4月15日起，Gemini Advanced用户可以通过Veo 2模型将文本提示转化为8秒高清视频，视频分辨率为720p，格式为MP4。Google One AI Premium用户则可通过Whisk Animate将图像生成8秒动画视频。Veo 2提升了视频生成的真实感和细节，支持多种风格和主题。用户可在Gemini应用中选择Veo 2，输入详细描述以生成视频，并可通过移动端分享至TikTok和YouTube Shorts等平台。Whisk Animate是Google Labs的实验项目，现向全球订阅用户开放。所有生成的视频都带有SynthID水印，以确保安全和透明。视频生成现已向全球Gemini Advanced用户推出，访问gemini.google.com即可体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google发布的Whisk等AI工具及其相关技术（如Imagen 3、Veo 2）的使用体验、技术实现、应用场景和存在的问题。

不同观点：
• 正面评价：
   - Whisk工具使用有趣且功能强大，尤其在图像转文本描述的"prompt transmutation trick"上有不错的表现（minimaxir）。
   - 认为当前是机器学习技术快速发展的时期，大公司之间的竞争推动了技术进步（byearthithatius）。
   - 对AI生成工具在创作中的潜力感到惊喜，特别是与Krita等传统工具结合的应用（xnx，volkk提供的正面例子）。

• 负面评价与问题反馈：
   - 使用Veo 2生成视频成本高昂，且因内容审核问题导致创作受限（pdntspa，deyiao，kumarm）。
   - 对文本生成工具的局限性感到失望，尤其是生成结果不理想时反复调整的挫败感（volkk）。
   - 工具的用户界面设计不直观，不同工作流程之间的整合不佳（bredren）。

• 技术与创作自由度的争议：
   - 质疑为何AI工具多为文本生成，并提出是否可以有更具创意控制力的工具（torginus）。
   - 希望有更接近传统创作工具（如手绘草图和关键帧编辑器）的AI工具，以实现更精细的创作控制（torginus）。

补充讨论：
• 对AI生成工具是否能真正帮助创意工作者的质疑，认为目前这些工具主要被用于生成短视频广告和网络垃圾内容（volkk）。
• 对计算资源消耗的疑问，比较AI视频生成与Blender渲染农场的计算需求（bk496）。
• 对AI视频生成工具保留原始图片特征的需求，认为当前工具（如Whisk）在生成过程中对原图的改动过大（hu3）。
• 对Google产品发布和命名混乱的抱怨，用户对不同模型和功能的访问权限不明确（Palmik，anonzzzies）。

43695592.article_content:
Generate videos in Gemini and Whisk with Veo 2
Apr 15, 2025
·
[[read-time]] min read
Share
Twitter
Facebook
LinkedIn
Mail
Copy link
Transform text-based prompts into high-resolution eight-second videos, accessible to Gemini Advanced subscribers. Plus, Google One AI Premium subscribers can use Whisk Animate to turn images into eight-second animated clips.
Angela Sun
Director of Multimodal Platforms, Gemini App
Olivia Sturman
Product Manager, Google Labs
Share
Twitter
Facebook
LinkedIn
Mail
Copy link
Sorry, your browser doesn't support embedded videos, but don't worry, you can
download it
and watch it with your favorite video player!
Starting today, Gemini Advanced users can generate and share videos using our state-of-the-art video model,
Veo 2
. In Gemini, you can now translate text-based prompts into dynamic videos. Google Labs is also making Veo 2 available through
Whisk
, a generative AI experiment that allows you to create new images using both text and image prompts, and now animate them into videos.
How to create videos with Gemini
Veo 2 represents a
leap forward
in video generation, designed to produce high-resolution, detailed videos with cinematic realism. By better understanding real-world physics and human motion, it delivers fluid character movement, lifelike scenes and finer visual details across diverse subjects and styles.
To generate videos, select Veo 2 from the model dropdown
1
in Gemini. This feature creates an eight-second video clip at 720p resolution, delivered as an MP4 file in a 16:9 landscape format. There is a monthly limit on how many videos you can create, but we will notify you as you approach it.
Creating videos
with Gemini is simple: just describe the scene you want to create — whether it's a short story, a visual concept, or a specific scene — and Gemini will bring your ideas to life. The more detailed your description, the more control you have over the final video. This opens up a world of fun creative possibilities, letting your imagination go wild to picture unreal combinations, explore varied visual styles from realism to fantasy, or quickly narrate short visual ideas.
One of the best parts of creating is sharing with others. Sharing your video on mobile is easy: simply tap the share button to quickly upload engaging short videos to platforms like TikTok and YouTube Shorts.
Prompt: A wide, slow-panning shot of an enormous glacial cavern, bathed in eerie twilight. Pale cyan light filters from above, illuminating frozen candy figures within the ice walls. Two figures in white exosuits, their helmet lights casting beams, trudge through the center. Capture the cavern's scale and stillness.
Prompt: An animated shot of a tiny mouse with oversized glasses, reading a book by the light of a glowing mushroom in a cozy forest den.
Prompt: Aerial shot of a grassy cliff onto a sandy beach where waves crash against the shore, a prominent sea stack rises from the ocean near the beach, bathed in the warm, golden light of either sunrise or sunset, capturing the serene beauty of the Pacific coastline.
Prompt: Time-lapse of a voxel-style ice cream melting under a clear blue sky. The pink, grey, and white scoops slowly lose their shape, dripping down the yellow, blocky cone held by a large, voxel hand with a blue sleeve. Focus on the melting process, highlighting the changing texture and form of the voxel elements as the ice cream deforms and drips, creating a colorful, pixelated melt against the vibrant blue backdrop.
Video generation is now rolling out to Gemini Advanced subscribers globally on web and mobile, starting today and continuing over the next few weeks. This feature is available in all languages Gemini supports. Try it out today at
gemini.google.com
.
How Whisk Animate brings your images to life
Introduced in December
, Whisk is a Google Labs experiment that helps you quickly explore and visualize new ideas using both text and image prompts. Today, you can animate your creations with Whisk Animate.
Whisk Animate lets you turn your images into vivid eight-second videos using Veo 2. It’s available for Google One AI Premium subscribers globally starting today. Subscribers can try it at
labs.google/whisk
.
How we approach safety
We’ve taken important steps to make video generation a safe experience. This includes extensive
red teaming
and evaluation aimed at preventing the generation of content that violates our
policies
. Additionally, all videos generated with Veo 2 are marked with
SynthID
, a digital watermark embedded in each frame, which indicates the videos are AI-generated.
Gemini's outputs are primarily determined by user prompts and like any generative AI tool, there may be instances where it generates content that some individuals find objectionable. We’ll continue to listen to your feedback through the thumbs up/down buttons and make ongoing improvements. For more details, you can
read about our approach on our website
.
We hope you enjoy making videos in the Gemini app

data.title: Clolog
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: Clolog 是一个嵌入在 Clojure 中的逻辑编程系统（类似于 Prolog），受 LogLisp、Lisp Machine Prolog 和 Franz Inc. 的 Allegro Prolog 启发，并提供了一些额外功能。它强调表达能力和执行透明度，支持快速原型设计和概念验证开发。Clolog 允许在 Clojure 中调用 Prolog 风格的逻辑推理，使用类似 Lisp 的语法。它支持逻辑变量、统一、否定推理、内置逻辑操作符（如 `and`、`or`、`not`）、用户自定义谓词转换等功能。系统还提供了对 Clojure 值的访问以及对谓词的全面控制（如 "leashing" 机制）。通过示例展示了如何进行断言、查询、执行带有副作用的操作以及复杂的逻辑控制流程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Clolog API的设计及其在Clojure中的使用

不同观点：
• Alex-Robbins认为Clolog的API过于命令式，依赖于全局状态和副作用，导致在REPL驱动的开发中失去了一些便捷性。他还担心多个部分的程序使用Clolog时可能出现的全局状态冲突问题，并指出需要通过动态绑定等方法来解决，但这增加了不必要的复杂性。
•Perdomon表示对Clolog不太熟悉，因为其背景主要来自Javascript和PHP，但对尝试Clolog充满期待。
•Mark_L_Watson对Clolog表示赞赏，认为Clojure项目命名具有吸引力，并在试用后给予积极评价。
•Sterlind欢迎逻辑编程的复兴，认为它在特定情况下是非常强大的工具。
•Anonzzzies分享了自己在Common Lisp中类似的开发经验，并对Clolog表示兴趣。
•Winwang表示Clolog可能成为其尝试Clojure的理由。
•Cpdean赞赏了Clolog的README文件的详尽性。
•AtlasBarfed提出了关于Prolog是否类似于SAT求解器的问题。
•Jdminhbg则提出了一个技术选择问题，询问在什么情况下选择Clolog而不是core.logic。

补充讨论：
•Alex-Robbins的评论引发了对Clolog API设计是否合适的深入讨论，特别是其全局状态管理和副作用的问题。
•多个评论者（Perdomon, Mark_L_Watson, Winwang等）表达了对Clojure和Clolog的兴趣和期待，显示出社区对新工具的开放态度。

43695620.article_summary: Clolog 是一个嵌入在 Clojure 中的逻辑编程系统（类似于 Prolog），受 LogLisp、Lisp Machine Prolog 和 Franz Inc. 的 Allegro Prolog 启发，并提供了一些额外功能。它强调表达能力和执行透明度，支持快速原型设计和概念验证开发。Clolog 允许在 Clojure 中调用 Prolog 风格的逻辑推理，使用类似 Lisp 的语法。它支持逻辑变量、统一、否定推理、内置逻辑操作符（如 `and`、`or`、`not`）、用户自定义谓词转换等功能。系统还提供了对 Clojure 值的访问以及对谓词的全面控制（如 "leashing" 机制）。通过示例展示了如何进行断言、查询、执行带有副作用的操作以及复杂的逻辑控制流程。

data.title: The case of the UI thread that hung in a kernel call
data.author: luu
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于线程暂停（suspend thread）的技术讨论，特别是在多运行时环境中的问题，以及由此引发的系统编程和调试的挑战。

不同观点：
• **Simscitizen**：指出在多运行时环境中，原生内存分配器和托管语言运行时的垃圾回收机制可能同时暂停线程，导致互相阻塞。他建议通过强制执行某种层次结构或互斥来解决此问题，但也承认在某些情况下暂停线程是必要的，例如垃圾回收（GC）算法。

• **Saagarjha**：回应了在某些平台（如iOS）上，无法轻松地从另一个进程捕获线程堆栈，因此必须在当前进程内暂停线程以捕获堆栈信息。虽然这种方法可能导致问题，但在实践中通过小心控制暂停时间，可以实现相对安全的实现。

• **Ot**：提到在Linux系统上，可以通过发送信号（signal）来暂停线程并捕获堆栈信息，并指出需要确保信号处理函数是异步信号安全的。他还询问了Windows系统中是否有类似的机制。

• **Rayao**：质疑哪些客户能够获得微软工程团队的开发者支持，暗示该支持可能不面向普通用户。

• **Zavec**：对文章标题和作者（推测为Raymond Chen）表示认可，认为Raymond的文章内容引人入胜。

• **Boxed**：分享了一个关于在国防公司遇到内核挂起问题的支持案例，该问题最终因使用旧编译器而关闭，暗示了系统编程中复杂问题的调试难度。

• **Permik**：幽默地猜测该客户可能是Valve公司。

• **Markus_zhang**：表示虽然不太理解技术细节，但Raymond的文章能安抚其编程中的困惑，并好奇该客户是否为游戏工作室。

• **Pitterpatter**：分享了一个设置界面挂起的bug案例，该问题由线程死锁引发，最终发现是由于缓冲区溢出导致的。

• **Frabona**：强调“不要暂停自己的线程”应该是每个Windows开发者的常识，并以幽默方式建议将其铭记于心。

• **Makz**：对文章标题和微软的关系表示理解，但最初感到困惑。

• **Rat87**：提到一个导致Windows蓝屏的bug，当在调试C#的Ping操作时停止Visual Studio调试时会发生该问题。

• **Baruchthescribe**：指出“暂停的UI线程表现为挂起”的描述不够准确，建议使用“停止响应”这一术语，并提到需要参考风格指南。

• **Brcmthrowaway**：询问Grand Central Dispatch（GCD）是否也会遇到类似的问题。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中涉及了多个操作系统的线程调试技术，包括Windows、Linux和iOS。
- 涉及了具体案例和实际调试经验，提供了对线程暂停问题实际影响的见解。
- 争议的焦点在于是否应完全避免在进程内暂停线程，以及在不同操作系统中处理此类问题的技术差异。
- 部分评论带有幽默和个人猜测，如对客户身份的调侃和对Raymond文章风格的赞赏。

data.title: Fun ways of deciding authorship order (2016)
data.author: qifzer
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了生态学和进化生物学领域中决定论文作者顺序的一些非传统方法。作者提到了一次通过推特引发的关于作者顺序的讨论，其中包括按字母顺序、篮球比赛、25局槌球系列赛、掷硬币、随机抽样、烘焙比赛（ brownie bake-off）等多种有趣的方式。例如，Young & Young（1992）通过烘焙比赛决定作者顺序，而Hassell & May（1974）通过槌球比赛决定。此外，文章还提到了一些因作者顺序引发的实际问题和争议，如一篇论文因作者顺序纠纷而被撤稿。作者呼吁开放科学，并邀请读者分享其他有趣的例子。文章最后指出，确定作者顺序有时比写作本身更费时。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：学术论文作者排序的多样性与争议

不同观点：
• **引入新方法**：[jpmattia] 提到了一种新的方法，即每位作者都是第一作者（Every Author as First Author），并提供了一篇相关论文链接（arXiv:2304.01393）。
• **领域差异**：[jghn] 指出不同学术领域的作者排序有不同的最佳实践，并认为这种差异虽然合理，但仍令人惊讶。
• **乐队类比**：[dhosek] 用90年代乐队的例子类比，描述了初始创意提出者为第一作者的做法，并提到自己作为"仁慈的独裁者"决定其他作者的顺序。
• **姓氏共享**：[setgree] 提到与同姓氏的人合作撰写论文，并引用了"A Few Goodmen: Surname-Sharing Economist Coauthors"作为例子，展示了这种合作现象。
• **字母顺序**：[tpoacher] 分享了一个按字母顺序排序作者的例子，并幽默地指出当自己的姓氏首字母靠后时的不公平感。
• **幽默定理**：[dfltr] 提到其伴侣所在的数学小组为了不偏离标准的字母顺序，能够创作一篇关于DILF定理的论文。
• **随机排序**：[hinkley] 引用了用R语言随机决定作者顺序的例子，并质疑谁选择了种子数以及是否有偏袒。
• **保持原样**：[MortyWaves] 决定在个人网站上按论文原始顺序列出作者，因为找不到可靠的排序方法。
• **资历排序**：[a_e_k] 提到在一个系统论文中，主作者之后按团队中资历递减排序作者。
• **平等贡献**：[Der_Einzige] 认为在AI/ML领域，使用"同等贡献"星号标注可以让多名作者技术上成为第一作者，以给予尽可能多的认可。

补充讨论：
• 不同学术领域的作者排序实践存在显著差异，许多人对此缺乏了解。
• 幽默和随机的方法被用来解决排序争议，如乐队类比、字母顺序和随机排序。
• 强调给予作者公平认可的不同尝试，如平等贡献标注。

43695285.article_content:
Last spring, I did a
poll related to authorship order in ecology
. I’ve written up a couple of posts presenting the results of that poll (
part 1
,
part 2
), and plan on writing more. But, for now, I want to focus on some . . . less standard ways of deciding authorship for ecology and evolutionary biology papers.
*
It all started with this tweet (which makes me also want to write a post with best opening lines of ecology & evolution papers — give suggestions in the comments!
**
):
https://twitter.com/SophieLGilbert/status/775747332285444096
My reply to that was that there’s another Hairston & Hairston paper (
1993
AmNat
)
where authorship was determined alphabetically:
I realize that it’s not that uncommon for folks to alphabetize authorship order, but it probably doesn’t usually require getting to the 21st letter of the name to break the tie!
That sparked this tweet about Fauth & Resetarits (
1991
Ecology
), which is what motivated this post:
I'm kind partial to the time when authorship was determined on the court
@ESA_org
pic.twitter.com/71C9HyoBvf
— Travis Ryan (@IndyWildWatch)
September 13, 2016
Authorship determined by basketball skills is certainly an early contender for most fun way of determining authorship order. That led me to ask on twitter for other examples . . . which got lots of replies!
It turns out there was precedent for using athletic pursuits to determine authorship order.
Hassell & May (1974,
J. Animal Ecology
)
chose authors based on a 25 game croquet series (ht: Robin Choudhury, Noam Ross, Adam Stuckert).
(Is croquet an athletic pursuit? Whatever, I’m sticking with it.)
Some choose to go with random approaches. There’s the classic coin flip, used by Miller & Ballard (
1992
Wildlife Society Bulletin
) and surely others (ht: Jeremy):
Or the more modern version:
Depending on your definition of "fun" I did
>set.seed(thatdaysdate) >sample(c('myname', 'theirname'), 1).
— Stats for bios (@StatsForBios)
September 19, 2016
However, sometimes geography makes a coin flip difficult, in which case authors use more creative approaches, as in the case of Feder & Mitchell-Olds (
2003,
Nature Reviews Genetics
) (ht: Stephen Heard, in his
book on writing
)
I wish they’d explained more!
Others have used very practical concerns to determine authorship order of Roderick & Gillespie (
1998
Molecular Ecology
) (ht: Jeremy, Stephen Heard)
And then there’s the chance to use game theory to figure out authorship order, as done by Riechert & Hammerstein (
1983
Annual Review of Ecology & Systematics
). (ht: Don Schoolmaster)
Or, one could go with the rock-paper-scissors approach, as used by Kupfer et al. (
2004
Agriculture, Ecosystems & Environment
) (ht: Stephen Heard, in his
book on writing
)
But all the ones above pale in comparison to this one by
Young & Young (1992
Ecology
)
:
That’s right: a brownie bake-off! (ht: Robin Choudhury, Ryan McEwen, Don Yee) The competition is over, folks! Clearly this is the best way to determine authorship order, and I’m happy to volunteer to judge these competitions, as a service to the field. Though, I fully agree with Jeff Hollister’s call for open science on this one:
https://twitter.com/jhollist/status/777946235441471488
Of course, even once you’ve determined authorship order, there are still other questions related to authorship that might need to be addressed.
***
It turns out that, if you feel your coauthors didn’t pull their weight, you can address that with a footnote, too, as done by Hendry et al. (2013
Evolutionary Ecology Research
).
If you know of others that I missed, please let me know!
Postscript:
Right as I finished this post, I learned (thanks to being tagged into a conversation on twitter by Stephanie Carlson) that a banjo played a key role in determining the order of authorship of Hilborn & Mangel’s
Ecological Detective
(which was one of the most popular responses in
Brian’s poll of favorite ecology books
). The story is told in a
piece by Hilborn
:
It is a very nice banjo!:
Banjo that resulted from  authorship order
pic.twitter.com/GOBPHcsHdC
— Marc Mangel (@MarcMangel1)
August 21, 2016

Here’s one from economics (ht: Emilio Bruna):
Sometimes the most time consuming part of writing a paper is determining the order of authorship.

43695285.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了生态学和进化生物学领域中决定论文作者顺序的一些非传统方法。作者提到了一次通过推特引发的关于作者顺序的讨论，其中包括按字母顺序、篮球比赛、25局槌球系列赛、掷硬币、随机抽样、烘焙比赛（ brownie bake-off）等多种有趣的方式。例如，Young & Young（1992）通过烘焙比赛决定作者顺序，而Hassell & May（1974）通过槌球比赛决定。此外，文章还提到了一些因作者顺序引发的实际问题和争议，如一篇论文因作者顺序纠纷而被撤稿。作者呼吁开放科学，并邀请读者分享其他有趣的例子。文章最后指出，确定作者顺序有时比写作本身更费时。

data.article_summary: Resonate是一种低延迟、低内存占用和低计算成本的算法，用于评估音频信号中的感知相关光谱信息。该算法基于共振器模型，利用指数加权移动平均（EWMA）在时域中累积信号贡献，通过复数描述共振频率的幅度。算法通过少量算术运算实时更新状态，适用于音频频率范围（20-20000 Hz）。其核心参数α控制系统动态，更新仅需处理当前样本，无需缓冲。共振器组可独立调谐，适应感知相关的频率尺度，计算复杂度与共振器数量线性相关，且支持并行计算。与FFT方法相比，Resonate提供更高时间分辨率和更相关频率分辨率的频谱图。相关代码和示例在开源项目noFFT和Oscillators中提供。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Resonate项目及其相关资源、技术细节和应用场景

不同观点：
• **arjf** 分享了Resonate网站上提供的资源，包括Oscillators应用程序、YouTube视频播放列表以及开源的Swift和Python代码库，以展示其实时频谱分析和音频特征提取功能。
• **drmikeando** 从数学角度详细解释了信号处理中的卷积积分，并说明如何将其离散化，提出了与Resonate网页上结果一致的推导过程。他还提到可以使用其他滤波器（如box filter或triangular filter）来代替指数衰减滤波器。
• **colanderman** 认为基于CQT（Constant-Q Transform）的分析工具优于基于STFT的工具（如Audacity），并表示希望将工具切换到基于gammatone滤波器的方法，但不确定如何实现高效处理。
• **james_a_craig** 指出了C++代码中Pi值的错误，实际值与代码中给出的值存在细微差别，这可能影响算法的精度。

• **dr_dshiv** 提到Resonate项目让他想起Helmholtz共振器，并分享了一篇关于共振的跨学科论文，可能对理解该项目有帮助。

• 讨论中涉及的技术细节包括卷积积分、指数衰减滤波器、gammatone滤波器、FFT算法、Z变换等。

43694157.article_content:
Resonate is a low latency, low memory footprint, and low computational cost algorithm to evaluate perceptually relevant spectral information from audio (and other) signals.
Overview
Resonate builds on a resonator model that accumulates the signal contribution around its resonant frequency in the time domain using the Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA), also known as a low-pass filter in signal processing. Consistently with on-line perceptual signal analysis, the EWMA gives more weight to recent input values, whereas the contributions of older values decay exponentially.
A compact, iterative formulation of the model affords computing an update at each signal input sample, requiring no buffering and involving only a handful of arithmetic operations.
Each resonator, characterized by its resonant frequency \(f = \frac{\omega}{2\pi}\), is described by a complex number \(R\) whose amplitude captures the contribution of the input signal component around frequency \(f\).
The formulas below capture the recursive update for \(R\) by way of a phasor \(P\), applied for each sample \(x\) of a real-valued input signal \(x(t) \in [-1,1]\), regularly sampled at sampling rate \(sr\). \(\Delta t=1/sr\) is the sample duration, and \(\alpha \in [0,1]\) is a constant parameter that dictates how much each new measurement affects the accumulated value.
\[P \leftarrow P e^{-i \omega \Delta t}\]
\[R \leftarrow (1-\alpha) R + \alpha x P\]
The two complex numbers \(P\) and \(R\) capture the full state of the resonator. Updating the state at each input signal sample only requires a handful of arithmetic operations. Calculating the power and/or magnitude is not necessary for the update, and can be carried out only when required by the application, relatively efficiently as well.
The single parameter \(\alpha\), which can be related to a time constant, governs the dynamics of the system. For the frequency range of interest in audio applications (20-20000 Hz), the function \(\alpha_f = 1-e^{-\Delta t\frac{f}{log(1+f)} }\) is a reasonable heuristic.
The smoothed state \(\tilde{R}\) is produced by applying the EMWA to \(R\) with the same \(\alpha\) to dampen power and phase oscillations.
Finally, the output of each resonator is optionally normalized by the total response across the bank to a step signal of the resonator’s frequency (equalization).
Banks of resonators, independently tuned to perceptually relevant frequency scales, compute an instantaneous, perceptually relevant estimate of the spectral content of an input signal in real-time.
Both memory and per-sample computational complexity of such a bank are linear in the number of resonators, and independent of the number of input samples processed, or duration of processed signal.
Furthermore, since the resonators are independent, there is no constraint on the tuning of their resonant frequencies or time constants, and all
per sample
computations can be parallelized across resonators.
In an offline processing context, the cumulative computational cost for a given duration increases linearly with the number of input samples processed.
Spectrograms
Spectral information as a function of time is typically presented graphically for human consumption in the form of a spectrogram, in which the horizontal axis represents time and the vertical axis represents frequency. The value at each point represents the power of the frequency in the input signal at the given time slice. These values are usually normalized by the maximum value over the signal, and mapped to a logarithmic color scale to produce plots like those shown below.
A Resonate oscillator bank with adequately tuned resonators computes an arbitrary frequency scale spectrogram directly and efficiently, with more relevant frequency resolution and much higher temporal resolutiont than FFT-based methods.
Log-frequency power spectrograms of
Librosa
's vibeace music example, computed from the constant-Q transform (CQT) and from a Resonate implementation (spectrogram display and CQT from Librosa, sampling rate: 22050Hz, hop length: 512 samples, 100 frequency bins from 32.7Hz to 9955.1Hz, 12 bins per octave).
Mel-frequency power spectrograms of
Librosa
's Libri3 speech sample, computed from the constant-Q transform (CQT) and from a Resonate implementation (spectrogram display and CQT from Librosa, sampling rate: 22050Hz, hop length: 32 samples, 128 frequency bins from 0 to 8000Hz).
Publications
Alexandre R.J. François,
“Resonate: Efficient Low Latency Spectral Analysis of Audio Signals,”
to appear in Proceedings of the 50th Anniversary of the International Computer Music Conference 2025,
Boston, MA, USA, 8-14 June 2025.
Resources
The open source python module
noFFT
provides python and C++ implementations of Resonate functions and Jupyter notebooks illustrating their use in offline settings.
The open source
Oscillators Swift package
contains reference implementations in Swift and C++.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对硬件问题在软件质量达到一定水平后成为主要"不可能" bug 来源的关注，特别是与处理器架构（如E-Core与P-Core Xeons）的关系，以及硬件错误的不同类型（如soft error与整个package失效）。

不同观点：
• electricshampo1认为，随着软件质量的提高，硬件问题（尤其是随机硬件问题）成为了导致难以排查的bug的主要原因，并特别指出集群核心的E-Core Xeon架构可能在解决这些问题上更具优势。相比之下，P-Core Xeon的每个物理核心相对独立，可能不利于这类问题的解决。

• trebligdivad质疑这种方法是否仅限于芯片内软核心的锁步（lockstep）机制，可以解决低级错误（如soft error），但如果整个处理器包（package）失效则无能为力。尽管如此，仍对该技术表示肯定。

• bombela提出了软件与硬件bug在实际应用中的比例问题，并建议相关研究可能会帮助产生这一指标，从而更好地理解硬件bug的普遍性。

补充讨论：
• 不同处理器架构（E-Core与P-Core）在应对硬件问题上的有效性成为讨论的焦点，尤其是核心架构设计对排查硬件bug的影响。
• 对硬件错误类型的区分（如soft error与package失效）引发了对现有技术解决方案适用范围的思考。
• 提出了软件和硬件bug在实际产品中的比例问题，强调了对这一指标进行量化研究的价值。

这篇文章介绍了如何在NixOS配置中实现随机数生成（RNG）和余弦函数。NixOS使用Nix语言进行系统配置，这种语言是纯函数式的，具有懒惰求值和动态类型特性。由于Nix的纯函数性质，它本身不支持RNG，但文章提供了一个通过读取`/proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid`和`/dev/random`生成随机数的复杂代码示例。

文章还讨论了Nix的缓存机制如何影响随机数生成，并提出使用当前时间作为随机种子的解决方案，尽管时间精度和纯评估模式下存在限制。最终，文章通过实验发现Nix中的字符串具有上下文，这影响了衍生结果的路径比较。为解决这些问题，文章建议在`configuration.nix`中启用实验性功能，如`nix-command`和`flakes`。

RNG and Cosine in Nix
How to implement random number generation and cosine for your NixOS configuration
12 min read |
April 12, 2025
nix
nixos
functional-programming
NixOS is an immutable, atomic Linux distribution with a declarative and reproducible configuration and packaging system using the purely functional, lazily evaluated, dynamically typed Nix programming language.
Kublai
: AAAAAAHHH too many buzzwords, what does that all mean???
Glad you asked! Basically, in NixOS, you can configure your entire system using a
configuration.nix
file and NixOS will magically (using a bunch of Bash scripts) figure out what needs to be installed and how to do it. For instance, if you want to enable Firefox, you’d add
programs.firefox.enable = true;
to your
configuration.nix
. Easy as that.
Kublai
: Sure that sounds cool, but what if I want to enable Firefox with only 50% probability?
Great question! The easiest solution would be something like
randomNumber = 4
(
from this xkcd
), but what about doing the RNG using the Nix language so that it’s
d
e
c
l
a
r
a
t
i
v
e
?
RNG
Sadly, Nix doesn’t have built-in RNG since it’s purely functional, but I found a project called
rand-nix
with this code:
let
pkgs
=
import
<nixpkgs>
{ };
seed
=
builtins
.
replaceStrings [
"-"
"
\n
"
] [
""
""
]
(builtins
.
readFile
/proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid
);
hash
=
builtins
.
hashString
"sha256"
;
rng
=
seed: pkgs
.
lib
.
fix (self: {
int
=
(builtins
.
fromTOML
"x=0x
${
builtins
.
substring
28
8
(hash seed)
}
"
)
.
x;
intBetween
=
x: y: x
+
pkgs
.
lib
.
mod self
.
int (y
-
x);
next
=
rng (hash seed);
skip
=
pkgs
.
lib
.
flip pkgs
.
lib
.
pipe [
(pkgs
.
lib
.
flip pkgs
.
lib
.
replicate (x: x
.
next))
(pkgs
.
lib
.
pipe self)
];
take
=

genList self
.

});
in
{
a
=
(rng seed)
.
int;
b
=
builtins

readFile
/proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid
;
}
Kublai
: Whoa, that’s a lot of code! What does it do?
Basically, it reads random data from
/proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid
, SHA256es it, and parses the hex string using
builtins.fromTOML
and does a bunch of other things that you don’t need to worry about. Anyways, let’s run it with
nix eval --file main.nix
and see what it prints out:
{ a
=
3106154414
; b
=
""
; }
SHL
: This post uses some experimental Nix features, so if you get any errors, add
nix.settings.experimental-features = ["nix-command" "flakes" "pipe-operators"];
to your
configuration.nix
. The new
nix
CLI is much better anyways.
Let’s try it again:
{ a
=
3106154414
; b
=
""
; }
Huh, that doesn’t look right. It’s printing out the same random number each time! And it seems like we can’t read anything from the
/proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid
file!
One solution to this is to use
pkgs.runCommandLocal
to get an environment where we can access
/proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid
or
/dev/random
which I’ll use here for simplicity:
seed
=
pkgs
.
runCommandLocal
"myCommand"
{}
"od -A n -t d -N 4 /dev/random > $out"
|
>
import
|
>
builtins
.
toString;
Yay, now we can access a file with some randomness in it! Sadly… this doesn’t exactly work either. Now the program prints out
1661889355
for me every time I run it!
This is because
pkgs.runCommandLocal
creates a Nix derivation which gets cached when we run it. For future runs, Nix will just use the cached value since it thinks this is a pure function! However, the caching depends on the name that we gave the derivation, in this case “myCommand”, so we just need to specify a random value each time we run this program. Easy as that… wait, where do we get that random value from? That’s what we’re trying to do in the first place!
Kublai
: I know, let’s use the current time!
Good thinking, Kublai. In Nix, we can obtain that using
builtins.currentTime
. However, this only gives us accuracy down to a second so if we run our program twice quickly, it’ll output the same thing. Also, this function isn’t available in
pure evaluation mode
. We’ll need some more creativity.
Caching… so troublesome… what if we could detect if we’re using a cached value or not? Let’s give that idea a try in
nix repl
.
nix-repl
>
builtins
.
pathExists (pkgs
.
runCommandLocal
"meow"
{}
"od -A n -t d -N 4 /dev/random > $out"
)
.
outPath
true
nix-repl
>
builtins
.
pathExists (pkgs
.
runCommandLocal
"meow2"
{}
"od -A n -t d -N 4 /dev/random > $out"
)
.
outPath
true
nix-repl
>
(pkgs
.
runCommandLocal
"meow3"
{}
"od -A n -t d -N 4 /dev/random > $out"
)
.
outPath
"/nix/store/hajf5106d42xh7h1amx8f32g6fl017gd-meow3"
nix-repl
>
builtins
.
pathExists
"/nix/store/hajf5106d42xh7h1amx8f32g6fl017gd-meow3"
false
nix-repl
>
(pkgs
.
runCommandLocal
"meow3"
{}
"od -A n -t d -N 4 /dev/random > $out"
)
.
outPath
==
"/nix/store/hajf5106d42xh7h1amx8f32g6fl017gd-meow3"
true
Huh? What’s going on?

: In Nix, strings aren’t just a bunch of characters but also have a
context
. The string from
.outPath
has an additional context that causes the derivation to be evaluated while the manually copied string doesn’t.

data.title: MeshCore, a new lightweight, hybrid routing mesh protocol for packet radios
data.author: cuu508
data.article_summary: **MeshCore** 是一个轻量级、可移植的 C++ 库，支持多跳包路由，适用于使用 LoRa 和其他包无线电的嵌入式项目。它旨在帮助开发者建立去中心化、具有弹性的通信网络，无需互联网。MeshCore 支持多种 LoRa 设备，可以通过工具（如 Adafruit ESPTool）刷入预构建的二进制文件，并通过串口与网络交互。其关键特性包括多跳包路由、支持 LoRa 无线电、低功耗和易于部署，适用于离网通信、应急响应、户外活动、物联网等场景。开发者可以通过 PlatformIO 开始使用，并选择聊天、中继器等示例应用。MeshCore 是开源软件，采用 MIT 许可协议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新 mesh 网络协议的应用和不同协议之间的比较

不同观点：
• apitman 认为新的 mesh 网络协议（如 Meshtastic 和 Reticulum）对于本地优先网络（local-first networking）和本地优先应用（local-first apps）非常重要。他还表达了对类似协议在 Bluetooth/WiFi 上实现的期待，并提到 WiFi Aware 可能是一个选择。

• sparrish 对 Meshtastic 和文中所提到的新协议之间的区别感到困惑，请求其他人帮助比较和区分这两者。

• Calwestjobs 指出 Meshtastic 计划支持更多无线电设备而不仅仅是 LoRa，并提到例如 ESP32 LoRa 节点可以用于高速度的 WiFi 传输，比如传输入侵者图片（半开玩笑）。他还强调了 Meshtastic 未来在多种无线电支持上的潜力。

• brunoqc 质疑 LoRa 等无线电技术是否真正适用于有用的文件传输，还是仅仅是一个玩具性质的技术。

补充讨论：
• 关于 Meshtastic 和其他新协议的具体区别是讨论的焦点之一。sparrish 要求澄清，而 Calwestjobs 提供了一些关于 Meshtastic 未来功能扩展的信息。
• brunoqc 对 LoRa 技术实用性的质疑引发了对无线电技术在实际应用中性能的讨论。
• apitman 提到了本地优先网络和本地优先应用的概念，暗示这些新技术可能在这些领域发挥重要作用。

About MeshCore
MeshCore is a lightweight, portable C++ library that enables multi-hop packet routing for embedded projects using LoRa and other packet radios. It is designed for developers who want to create resilient, decentralized communication networks that work without the internet.
🔍 What is MeshCore?
MeshCore now supports a range of LoRa devices, allowing for easy flashing without the need to compile firmware manually. Users can flash a pre-built binary using tools like Adafruit ESPTool and interact with the network through a serial console.
MeshCore provides the ability to create wireless mesh networks, similar to Meshtastic and Reticulum but with a focus on lightweight multi-hop packet routing for embedded projects. Unlike Meshtastic, which is tailored for casual LoRa communication, or Reticulum, which offers advanced networking, MeshCore balances simplicity with scalability, making it ideal for custom embedded solutions., where devices (nodes) can communicate over long distances by relaying messages through intermediate nodes. This is especially useful in off-grid, emergency, or tactical situations where traditional communication infrastructure is unavailable.
⚡ Key Features
Multi-Hop Packet Routing – Devices can forward messages across multiple nodes, extending range beyond a single radio's reach. MeshCore supports up to a configurable number of hops to balance network efficiency and prevent excessive traffic.
Supports LoRa Radios – Works with Heltec, RAK Wireless, and other LoRa-based hardware.
Decentralized & Resilient – No central server or internet required; the network is self-healing.
Low Power Consumption – Ideal for battery-powered or solar-powered devices.
Simple to Deploy – Pre-built example applications make it easy to get started.
🎯 What Can You Use MeshCore For?
Off-Grid Communication: Stay connected even in remote areas.
Emergency Response & Disaster Recovery: Set up instant networks where infrastructure is down.
Outdoor Activities: Hiking, camping, and adventure racing communication.
Tactical & Security Applications: Military, law enforcement, and private security use cases.
IoT & Sensor Networks: Collect data from remote sensors and relay it back to a central location.
🚀 How to Get Started
Andy Kirby has published a very useful
intro video
which explains the steps for beginners.
For developers, install
PlatformIO
in Visual Studio Code.
Download & Open the MeshCore repository.
Select a Sample Application: Choose from chat, repeater, other example app.
Monitor & Communicate using the Serial Monitor (e.g., Serial USB Terminal on Android).
📁 Included Example Applications
📡 Terminal Chat: Secure text communication between devices.
📡 Simple Repeater: Extends network coverage by relaying messages.
📡 Companion Radio: For use with an external chat app, over BLE or USB.
📡 Room Server: A simple BBS server for shared Posts.
🛠 Hardware Compatibility
MeshCore is designed for use with:
Heltec V3 LoRa Boards
RAK4631
XiaoS3 WIO (sx1262 combo)
XiaoC3 (plus external sx126x module)
LilyGo T3S3
Heltec T114
Station G2
Sensecap T1000e
Heltec V2
LilyGo TLora32 v1.6
📜 License
MeshCore is open-source software released under the MIT License. You are free to use, modify, and distribute it for personal and commercial projects.
Contributing
Please submit PR's using 'dev' as the base branch!
For minor changes just submit your PR and I'll try to review it, but for anything more 'impactful' please open an Issue first and start a discussion. Is better to sound out what it is you want to achieve first, and try to come to a consensus on what the best approach is, especially when it impacts the structure or architecture of this codebase.
📞 Get Support
Check out the GitHub Issues page to report bugs or request features.
You will be able to find additional guides and components at
my site
, or
join Andy Kirby's Discord
for discussions.

data.title: Cohere Launches Embed 4
data.author: rekovacs
data.article_summary: Cohere团队于2025年4月15日发布了Embed 4，这是一款提供先进准确性和效率的工具，帮助企业安全地检索多模态数据，以构建具有自主性的人工智能应用。该产品旨在提升企业在处理和利用复杂数据方面的能力，支持多种数据模式的搜索和整合。Embed 4的推出标志着企业在人工智能技术应用上的又一重要里程碑。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cohere嵌入模型的评价与争议

不同观点：
• Simonw：对Cohere表示尊重，但担心其专有嵌入模型只能通过API使用，不如Nomic的开放权重模型有长期使用的保障。Simonw欣赏Nomic的模型发布方式，既可以通过API使用，也可以在非商业用途下使用开放权重，后期还会重新授权旧模型。
• Xfalcox：因为Cohere没有可下载的开放权重，所以选择继续使用bge-m3模型。
• Tiffanyh：对Cohere的具体业务模式感到困惑，质疑他们的竞争优势以及与AWS的区别。
• Podgietaru：分享了自己使用Cohere构建RSS Reader / Aggregator的经历，认为Cohere价格便宜且在分类任务中表现出色，并提供了开源项目链接。
• Lukebuehler：指出多模态嵌入模型选择有限，Google模型支持的文本token数量太少，对Cohere的模型表示欢迎，并询问类似强大的嵌入模型推荐。
• Neom：质疑Cohere的长期价值主张，尽管在企业市场表现良好，但对其未来发展空间存疑。
• Pencildiver：高度评价Cohere，分享了自己在生产环境中使用Cohere V3和V4模型的经验，认为V4模型能提高搜索速度并解决多模态数据的边缘情况。
• Moojacob：对Cohere模型的基准测试表现持怀疑态度，认为基准测试对嵌入模型的实用性有限。
• BrandiATMuhkuh：对Cohere模型在处理复杂文档数据（如图纸、平面图等）方面的能力表示期待，认为这将大大改善当前数据处理的混乱状况。
• Cahaya：询问Cohere模型与Gemini嵌入模型的对比，特别是性能表现，指出缺乏MTEB评分难以比较。
• Moralestapia：认为Cohere模型价格偏高，但基准测试表现不错。
• Distantsounds：质疑Cohere模型训练数据是否包含侵权内容。

补充讨论：
• 关于Cohere模型的长期使用保障和开放权重的讨论，主要集中在Simonw和Xfalcox的观点中。
• 对Cohere商业模式和竞争优势的质疑，主要来自Tiffanyh和Neom。
• 实际使用经验的分享，如Podgietaru和Pencildiver，提供了Cohere在具体项目中的应用实例和性能评价。
• 对基准测试和模型性能的争议，主要体现在Moojacob和Cahaya的评论中，特别是与其他模型的比较。
• 对模型训练数据合法性的质疑，由Distantsounds提出。

争议焦点：
• Cohere模型的专有性和长期使用保障问题。
• Cohere的商业模式和竞争优势。
• 基准测试的实用性和模型性能的比较。
• 模型训练数据的合法性和潜在侵权问题。

• Neom：质疑Cohere的长期价值主张，尽管在企业市场表现良好，但对其未来发展空间存疑。
• Pencildiver：高度评价Cohere，分享了自己在生产环境中使用Cohere V3和V4模型的经验，认为V4模型能提高搜索速度并解决多模态数据的边缘情况。
• Moojacob：对Cohere模型的基准测试表现持怀疑态度，认为基准测试对嵌入模型的实用性有限。
• BrandiATMuhkuh：对Cohere模型在处理复杂文档数据（如图纸、平面图等）方面的能力表示期待，认为这将大大改善当前数据处理的混乱状况。
• Cahaya：询问Cohere模型与Gemini嵌入模型的对比，特别是性能表现，指出缺乏MTEB评分难以比较。
• Moralestapia：认为Cohere模型价格偏高，但基准测试表现不错。
• Distantsounds：质疑Cohere模型训练数据是否包含侵权内容。

补充讨论：
• 关于Cohere模型的长期使用保障和开放权重的讨论，主要集中在Simonw和Xfalcox的观点中。
• 对Cohere商业模式和竞争优势的质疑，主要来自Tiffanyh和Neom。
• 实际使用经验的分享，如Podgietaru和Pencildiver，提供了Cohere在具体项目中的应用实例和性能评价。
• 对基准测试和模型性能的争议，主要体现在Moojacob和Cahaya的评论中，特别是与其他模型的比较。
• 对模型训练数据合法性的质疑，由Distantsounds提出。

争议焦点：
• Cohere模型的专有性和长期使用保障问题。
• Cohere的商业模式和竞争优势。
• 基准测试的实用性和模型性能的比较。
• 模型训练数据的合法性和潜在侵权问题。

data.title: A Passion for Fruit
data.author: diodorus
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了水果在人类历史中的重要性。早在7000年前，人们就开始栽培各种水果，如果香蕉、无花果和鳄梨。考古学家通过发现古代水果的种子或果核，揭示了过去人们的创新和生活方式。例如，有人用蜂蜜保存无花果作为冬季的珍贵热量来源。水果不仅提供了糖分和营养，还带来了不同的风味和质地，一直是人们饮食中的重要部分。文章还介绍了全球不同地区与水果相关的历史和文化，如果部落在葬礼中使用水果，以及有毒水果的危险。总之，水果的多样性和历史反映了人类长期以来的实验和热爱。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：传统水果种植系统的创新性和可持续性

不同观点：
• 一些评论者（如barathr）认为，人们长期以来已经建立了富有创造性的水果种植系统，例如通过使用果墙（fruit walls）和太阳能等传统技术。这些系统展示了人类在农业方面的创新能力，并强调了古老方法在可持续农业中的潜力。
   
• 另一部分评论者指出，虽然这些传统方法展示了创新性，但在现代大规模农业中应用可能面临挑战。现代农业技术更为高效，能够满足全球人口增长带来的食物需求，而传统方法可能无法达到同样的生产规模。

• 有评论者提到，现代农业确实有其优势，但结合传统方法中的可持续理念，可以发展出更为环保和高效的混合农业模式。例如，利用果墙来调节温度、增加微气候效应，以提高水果质量和产量。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论讨论了低技术杂志（Low-tech Magazine）上提到的果墙技术的具体例子，例如在城市环境中通过建造墙体来吸收和释放热量，从而延长水果生长期。
   
• 争议的焦点在于传统农业方法能否在现代农业中得到广泛应用，尤其是在面对气候变化和资源有限的情况下，如何平衡传统智慧与现代科技的关系。

• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是关于可持续性的定义，部分人认为可持续农业不仅仅要考虑环境影响，还要考虑经济可行性和社会接受度。

A 15th-century manuscript shows trees bearing (clockwise from top left): sweet apples, jujubes, lemons, cherries, dates, and sour apples.
By 7,000 years ago
, people in New Guinea were cultivating bananas. Around the same time, figs in the Near East and avocados in Mesoamerica were well on their way to becoming the fruits we savor today. People across the world consume an astonishing variety of fruits. These range from the smallest edible example—a neon green sphere produced by the Asian watermeal plant that measures less than the width of a pencil tip—to the largest, the 100-pound yellowish-green jackfruit. “The fruit we eat now is a result of people experimenting extensively for thousands of years,” says archaeobotanist Erica Rowan of Royal Holloway.
For archaeologists, evidence of ancient fruit opens unexpected pathways to understanding the past. “The seeds or pits of fruit are quite hardy and survive well in the archaeological record,” says Rowan. Studying fruit can give scholars glimpses of the ingenuity of ancient peoples—for example, some used figs preserved in honey as a source of precious calories during harsh winters. People of all eras, it seems, have coveted fruit as a welcome departure from ordinary fare. “Fruit was used as a source of sugar, nutrients, flavor, and lots of different textures,” says Rowan. “Fruit was everywhere, all the time. It has always been very important to people.”

data.title: Isolated Execution Environment for eBPF
data.author: tuananh
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了由eBPF基金会资助的一个研究项目，旨在解决eBPF验证器面临的安全漏洞和复杂性问题。eBPF作为Linux内核的关键技术，其程序在执行前需经过静态验证。为提高安全性与可扩展性，研究团队提出将eBPF程序视为需要隔离的内核模式应用，并引入新的执行环境。文章详细分析了Linux v6.16中eBPF验证器的工作流程，包括预处理、控制流图检查和全路径分析三个阶段。团队通过自顶向下和自底向上的方法，手动分析验证器的设计，识别出多种安全检查，并区分出复杂性检查与安全性检查。研究重点在于全路径分析中的安全属性，以确保内存安全和控制流完整性。后续文章将讨论设计方法、当前进展及面临的挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：eBPF代码的隔离执行环境及其安全性和实现难度

不同观点：
• [skywhopper] 认为文章没有清楚地提出所谓的“隔离执行环境”的具体方案。文章主要讨论了早期验证eBPF代码的困难，但并没有详细解释为什么放宽“隔离”是一个合适的解决方案。作者提到“JavaScript做了类似的事情”，但JavaScript并不在 kernel 中运行。因此，文章没有充分说明为何放宽限制值得去冒安全性和可靠性风险。

• [westurner] 引用了其他讨论中的问题，探讨了微内核是否能够运行eBPF或WASM。他认为在 kernel 中运行eBPF有显著的性能优势，但同时也提出了关于内核或微内核应该承担多少功能的疑问。

补充讨论：
• [skywhopper] 强调了对在 kernel 中放宽隔离限制的担忧，认为文章没有充分讨论这样做可能带来的安全漏洞和可靠性问题。
• [westurner] 则更关注于技术实现的可能性和性能优势，提出了eBPF和WASM在微内核环境中的应用潜力。

争议焦点：
• 是否应该在 kernel 中放宽eBPF的隔离限制以解决当前的实现困难。
• 放宽隔离限制是否会导致严重的安全性和可靠性问题，以及如何避免这些问题。

43694431.article_content:
The post below is an update on a
research project sponsored by the eBPF Foundation
. It is the first in a series of posts about this research. The post was prepared by Zhe Wang (Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences; wangzhe12@ict.ac.cn), and Patrick Peihua Zhang (WeChat, Tencent; patrickzhang2333@gmail.com). Read about the status of all the sponsored research projects in
this post
.
1.   Project Overview
eBPF has evolved into a foundational technology in the Linux kernel, powering diverse subsystems from networking to observability. To safeguard kernel integrity, BPF programs undergo static verification before execution. However, the eBPF verifier faces challenges—security vulnerabilities and inherent complexity—that undermine its reliability.
In response, we propose a paradigm shift: redefining BPF programs as kernel-mode applications requiring dedicated isolation. This project introduces a novel execution environment designed to isolate BPF programs, offering an alternative architectural solution to enhance the security and scalability of eBPF infrastructure.
We systematically analyzed the eBPF verifier’s objectives to achieve equivalent security guarantees. This post serves as the first installment in our series, providing a structured summary of the verifier’s security guarantees in Linux v6.16. We focus specifically on unprivileged programs, as their requirements subsume those of privileged programs.
In subsequent blogs, we will discuss our design methodologies—including hardware-assisted and Software-Based Fault Isolation (SFI) approaches—alongside current milestones, challenges, and future directions.
2.   Verifier Workflow
Fig. 1 The workflow of the verifier.
The workflow of the verifier consists of three consecutive stages, with the later stages becoming more complex. As shown in Fig.1, the pre-processing stage scans the BPF program linearly to find relocation items and check for any unallowed opcodes, e.g., indirect calls (calls). The CFG check stage searches the control flow graph and forbids any out-of-bounds jumps or unreachable codes, thus ensuring the control flow integrity.
The last stage creates a state machine that records the type and range of all registers and stack slots during the path exploration. Meanwhile, it verifies that all states conform to a set of security properties that do not threaten the kernel, thus, e.g., ensuring memory safety. Since it traverses all possible paths, we call it full-path analysis. The full-path analysis performs most of the analysis and integrates the majority of security checks; focusing on it allows for a comprehensive understanding of the verifier’s capabilities and limitations.
3.   The Internals of Full-path Analysis
3.1 The Methodology of Study
Due to the lack of comprehensive documentation discussing the verifier, we had to understand its design manually. To this end, we undertook a top-down analysis from the verifier’s entry to all exits. We collected all checks and scrutinized the triggering conditions, the check’s content, its dependencies, and restrictions. To ensure comprehensiveness, we also performed a bottom-up analysis, beginning with all the verifier’s error messages to ensure no checks were overlooked.
All checks share a distinguishing feature: a conditional judgment statement with an error message output (e.g.,
verbose
()). Some of these checks are not related to the full-path analysis. For example, the division-by-zero check checks if the
imm
operand in the instruction is 0. Filtering such checks is simple by inspecting whether the condition contains the
env
. This is due to the program state used in the state machine being recorded in the verifier’s environment structure (
struct bpf_verifier_env *env
).
Among all the checks, some are complexity or functionality checks, such as the combined branch state cannot exceed
8,192
to prevent state explosion. We filter these checks by understanding their semantics, supplemented by the error message. For example, these checks usually contained phrases like “too many” or “too complex”. Conversely, the security checks typically contained “prohibited” or “invalid”. By understanding the filtered security checks and their semantics, we obtain all the security properties the verifier wants to ensure in the full-path analysis.
3.2 The Security Properties in Full-path Analysis
Fig. 2 The security checks and corresponding security properties in the full-path analysis.
Fig.2 gives a panoramic view of how the verifier performs the security checks in the full-path analysis. The
bpf_check
() function is the entry point of the verifier, and the
do_check
() it calls contains most of the security checks. We call them
inflight checks
since they are performed during the path traversal along with the state tracking. Whenever an instruction is encountered, it will perform security checks based on the semantics of the instruction and all operands’ states (i.e., the type and the value rang

data.title: JSX over the Wire
data.author: danabramov
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了一种不同寻常的方法，将API返回的数据直接以JSX形式提供给React组件。通常，API返回JSON数据，前端组件通过数据获取库将这些数据传递给子组件。文章提出，既然API返回的数据最终要成为组件的属性（props），为什么不直接在API中返回JSX组件？

文章首先展示了一个典型的API路由，返回JSON格式的点赞数据。接着，作者提出一个设想：如果API直接返回填充好数据的React组件，例如`<LikeButton />`，这样“父组件”就变成了API本身。这种方法颠倒了组件和API之间的关系，类似于“好莱坞原则”：“不要打电话给我，我会打给你。”

文章进一步分析了数据存储（Model）和展示（ViewModel）之间的区别，指出ViewModel是根据用户个性化聚合和处理后的数据形式。通常，Model需要转换为ViewModel，关键在于这个转换过程发生在哪里和如何演变。

这种方法虽然新奇，但文章提醒读者后续再考虑其优劣。

主要讨论点：React服务器组件（RSC）及其与其他技术（如HTMX、Phoenix LiveView、Inertia.js等）的比较和应用场景

不同观点：
• mattbessey：认为文章很好地阐述了RSC的特点，并通过Remix和htmx等工具的比较，认可RSC或类似技术可能是未来方向。同时对一些评论者未仔细阅读文章表示失望。
• jonathanhefner：赞赏RSC的强大功能，尤其是其作为序列化格式的优势。但他更关注在React中通过服务器函数返回组件的功能，并提出了自己的开源项目作为示例，希望React能原生支持类似功能。
• skydhash：对服务器端JSX持怀疑态度，认为这是不必要的抽象，增加了复杂性，主张保持前后端的分离，并通过JSON或HTML进行简单的数据交换。
• h14h：对RSC和Phoenix LiveView的比较感兴趣，特别是它们在处理客户端驱动mutation时的不同方法，并提出了一系列具体场景下的问题。
• android521：简单赞赏文章的高质量。

43694681.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了一种不同寻常的方法，将API返回的数据直接以JSX形式提供给React组件。通常，API返回JSON数据，前端组件通过数据获取库将这些数据传递给子组件。文章提出，既然API返回的数据最终要成为组件的属性（props），为什么不直接在API中返回JSX组件？

文章首先展示了一个典型的API路由，返回JSON格式的点赞数据。接着，作者提出一个设想：如果API直接返回填充好数据的React组件，例如`<LikeButton />`，这样“父组件”就变成了API本身。这种方法颠倒了组件和API之间的关系，类似于“好莱坞原则”：“不要打电话给我，我会打给你。”

文章进一步分析了数据存储（Model）和展示（ViewModel）之间的区别，指出ViewModel是根据用户个性化聚合和处理后的数据形式。通常，Model需要转换为ViewModel，关键在于这个转换过程发生在哪里和如何演变。

这种方法虽然新奇，但文章提醒读者后续再考虑其优劣。

data.article_summary: 2025年4月8日，货币监理署（OCC）向国会通报了一起重大信息安全事件。2月11日，OCC发现其办公自动化系统中的管理账户与用户邮箱存在异常互动，经确认后于2月12日启动应急响应，禁用了被入侵的管理账户并通报相关部门。2月26日，OCC公开了此事件。经分析，未经授权访问涉及高度敏感的金融信息，OCC已聘请第三方进行全面调查和安全评估，并计划改进IT安全政策和流程，确保类似事件不再发生。OCC正与财政部合作处理此事。

News Release 2025-30
|
April 8, 2025
OCC Notifies Congress of Incident Involving Email System
Share This Page:
WASHINGTONâThe Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) today notified Congress of a major information security incident, as required by the Federal Information Security Modernization Act.
This finding is the result of internal and independent third-party reviews of OCC emails and email attachments that were subject to unauthorized access. On February 11, 2025, the OCC learned of unusual interactions between a system administrative account in its office automation environment and OCC user mailboxes. On February 12, the OCC confirmed the activity was unauthorized and immediately activated its incident response protocols which include initiating an independent third-party incident assessment and reporting the incident to the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. On February 12, the OCC disabled the compromised administrative accounts and confirmed that the unauthorized access had been terminated. The OCC provided
public notice
of the incident on February 26.
After confirming the unauthorized activity, the OCC immediately began analyzing the compromised email messages to determine their contents. These efforts included using internal data science experts and independent third-parties and are ongoing. While that review is ongoing, based on the content of the emails and attachments reviewed thus far, the OCC, in consultation with the Department of the Treasury, determined the incident met the conditions necessary to be classified as a major incident.
The OCC discovered that the unauthorized access to a number of its executivesâ and employeesâ emails included highly sensitive information relating to the financial condition of federally regulated financial institutions used in its examinations and supervisory oversight processes.
âThe confidentiality and integrity of the OCCâs information security systems are paramount to fulfilling its mission,â said Acting Comptroller of the Currency Rodney E. Hood. âI have taken immediate steps to determine the full extent of the breach and to remedy the long-held organizational and structural deficiencies that contributed to this incident. There will be full accountability for the vulnerabilities identified and any missed internal findings that led to the unauthorized access.â
The OCC has utilized third-party cybersecurity experts to perform a full review of the investigation and forensics efforts. The OCC is also launching an immediate and thorough evaluation of its current IT security policies and procedures to improve its ability to prevent, detect and remediate potential security incidents going forward. In addition, the OCC is working to engage an additional independent third-party to assess and analyze internal processes related to cyber incidents.
Throughout its review, the OCC has coordinated with the Department of the Treasury to share information about its findings.

data.author: Anon84
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了57岁的德国妇女Sabine Fischer-Kugler为了避免长期透析，选择到肯尼亚进行非法肾脏移植的经历。在德国等待肾源需要多年，她通过中介前往肯尼亚，支付高额费用获得了一个来自高加索地区年轻男子的肾脏。文章揭示了全球非法器官交易的内幕，患者和贫困的供体在绝望中参与其中，中介和医生借此牟取暴利。这种不道德的“肾脏资本主义”生意在暗网上公然运作，尽管法律明令禁止。Fischer-Kugler明知过程不合法，但为了生存选择沉默，对供体的情况毫不关心。文章警示了全球器官交易的黑暗面及其对道德和法律的挑战。

主要讨论点：欧洲国家对"cookie墙"（即网站要求用户同意被追踪的机制）的不同政策及其效果

不同观点：
• [rkagerer的观点] 认为在没有"cookie墙"的情况下，用户能够更自由地访问内容，而不必被迫同意被追踪。他们引用了一个具体例子，展示了在没有"cookie墙"时的访问情况。

• [kelseyfrog的观点] 指出，像德国这样的"选择性加入"（opt-in）国家，用户的同意率较低，例如只有12%的用户选择允许被追踪。相比之下，邻国奥地利采用"选择性退出"（opt-out）机制，用户的同意率高达99%。这表明不同政策对用户同意被追踪的比例有显著影响。

补充讨论：
• [kelseyfrog提供的论据] 提供了维基百科链接和纽约时报的存档，以支持其关于德国和奥地利在用户追踪同意率上的差异。这表明政策的不同设计对用户行为的巨大影响。

• [争议焦点] 核心争议在于"选择性加入"（opt-in）和"选择性退出"（opt-out）机制的优劣。前者给予用户更多自主选择权，但可能导致企业获取的用户数据大幅减少；后者则更容易让企业获得用户数据，但可能在用户不知情或未明确同意的情况下侵犯隐私。

• [政策影响] 讨论还涉及到政策对用户行为和企业数据收集的影响，特别是在不同国家的对比中，如何在保护用户隐私和满足企业数据需求之间找到平衡。

The shock. That is perhaps the best place to start. The realization that time had run out. For her kidney and for life as she had known it. The letter arrived on May 23, 2022, and it marked the end of the almost 30 years she had lived with her first donor kidney. The envelope contained the results of a blood test. Her creatinine value was 3.6, far above the norm of around 1. She knew then that the organ wouldn’t last much longer.
Sabine Fischer-Kugler hung on for another year, as she recalls – drinking less and consuming less protein and potassium. Then, her doctor called with new test results. Her creatinine level was now over 6. The doctor told her to get ready and the taxi arrived half an hour later to take her to the place she had never wanted to return: the dialysis station. Three times a week, five hours each time. For several years, most likely – as long as it would take to slowly climb the long waiting list in Germany of thousands of people waiting for a new kidney, growing weaker all the while.
DER SPIEGEL 16/2025
The article you are reading originally appeared in German in issue 16/2025 (April 12th, 2025) of DER SPIEGEL.
SPIEGEL International
Perhaps that is the right way to start to understand just how far a person is willing to go to get a new kidney. All the way to Kenya. All the way to the outer limits of morality – and beyond. And how far a new kidney must travel such that Sabine Fischer-Kugler, 57 years old, can continue living as before. In her case, it was a kidney from the Caucasus in the body of a young man who flew to Kenya to have it removed so that he could then fly home presumably with a couple of thousand euros in his pocket.
Bild vergrößern
Sabine Fischer-Kugler is aware that it's not all perfectly legit.
Foto: Maria Bayer / DER SPIEGEL
"Why not look abroad? The main thing is I once again have a kidney and don’t have to go back on dialysis,” says Fischer-Kugler, back in her living room in northern Bavaria six weeks later. Her surgery took place on February 4, and everything has been great since then. Her creatinine value is back to 0.67. "It’s a young kidney, as you can immediately see in the ultrasound. It’s totally healthy.” And how is the donor doing, down to just one kidney, six weeks later? She doesn’t know. She doesn’t even know the donor’s name, nor does she want to.
That, too, is part of the story when a kidney becomes just another commodity, when supply and demand is dictated by desperation on both sides, when unscrupulous middlemen and doctors extract money from the global system of kidney capitalism. It is a business that is just as incompatible with too much knowledge as it is with too much conscience. One that operates because of the need, and because of the benefits and the profits it produces.
DER SPIEGEL, German public broadcaster ZDF and Deutsche Well teamed up over the course of several months to follow the organ trail. From Germany and Poland via Israel to the clinic in Eldoret, Kenya, that is currently in the center of an international and seemingly criminal kidney trade. The transactions and transplants link patients in Germany with donors in Caucasus nations like Azerbaijan. And it links prosperous Somalians with young Kenyans who are talked into earning a quick 2,000 to 5,000 euros for one of their kidneys, while patients in the West pay up to 200,000 euros to the organ traders – preferably in cash.
Bild vergrößern
Sabine Fischer-Kugler's photo album from Kenya
Foto: Maria Bayer / DER SPIEGEL
Kidneys from the Online Shop
It all sounds like a shadowy industry, well out of the public eye and so secret that one might think even the operating room lights have to be dimmed. But that is not the case. Kidneys from Kenya are offered openly on the internet – in German on a website registered in Germany. An Introduction to Modern CMake
Contents
An Introduction to Modern CMake
#
People love to hate build systems.
Just watch the talks from CppCon17 to see examples of developers making the state of build systems the brunt of jokes.
This raises the question: Why?
Certainly there are no shortage of problems when building.
But I think that we have a very good solution to quite a few of those problems.
It’s CMake. Not CMake 2.8 though; that was released before C++11 even existed!
Nor the horrible examples out there for CMake (even those posted on KitWare’s own tutorials list).
I’m talking about Modern CMake. CMake 3.15+, maybe even CMake 4.0+!
It’s clean, powerful, and elegant, so you can spend most of your time coding, not adding lines to an unreadable, unmaintainable Make (Or CMake 2) file.
Attention
This book is meant to be a living document. You can raise an issue or put in a merge request on
GitLab
.
You can also
download a copy as a PDF
. Be sure to check the
HSF CMake Training
, as well!
In short, here are the most likely questions in your mind if you are considering Modern CMake:
Why do I need a good build system?
#
Do any of the following apply to you?
You want to avoid hard-coding paths
You need to build a package on more than one computer
You want to use CI (continuous integration)
You need to support different OSs (maybe even just flavors of Unix)
You want to support multiple compilers
You want to use an IDE, but maybe not all of the time
You want to describe how your program is structured logically, not flags and commands
You want to use a library
You want to use tools, like Clang-Tidy, to help you code
You want to use a debugger
If so, you’ll benefit from a CMake-like build system.
Why must the answer be CMake?
#
Build systems are a hot topic. Of course there are many options. But even a really good one, or one that re-uses a familiar syntax, can’t come close to CMake.
Why?
Support.
Every IDE supports CMake (or CMake supports that IDE).
More packages use CMake than any other system.
So, if you use a library that is designed to be included in your code, you have a choice: Make your own build system, or use one of the provided ones, and that will almost always include CMake.
And that will quickly be the common denominator if you include multiple projects.
And, if you need a library that’s preinstalled, the chances of it having a find CMake script or config CMake script are excellent.
Shouldn’t I support the oldest version possible?
#
Short answer: No.
If you set your minimum version of CMake too low, CMake will produce a warning
or even an error. The oldest you can set it to is 3.5, with anything under 3.10
producing a warning, as of CMake 4.0 While a user can workaround this in
emergencies by setting
CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM
to a valid version, you
don’t want users to have to do that.
You really should
at least
use a version of CMake that came out after your
compiler, since it needs to know compiler flags, etc, for that version.  And,
since CMake will dumb itself down to the minimum required version in your CMake
file, installing a new CMake, even system wide, is pretty safe.  You should
at
least
install it locally.  It’s easy (1-2 lines in many cases), and you’ll
find that 5 minutes of work will save you hundreds of lines and hours of
CMakeLists.txt
writing, and will be much easier to maintain in the long run.
Quick summary of good minimums (more detail in book):
3.24: The package finding system is great, good minimum to support package authors.
3.18: Pretty good support for Python and CUDA, most systems have at least this.
3.15: This is as low as most projects should go, Ubuntu 20.04+ has 3.16+.
3.10: Lowest version to avoid a CMake warning, Ubuntu 18.04+.
3.5: If you
really
need it.
As long as you set a maximum version, you can even set minimums below this. But don’t.
Always set the maximum version to the highest version you test (like 4.0).
This will continue to work until CMake drops the
maximum
version from it’s
support window, rather than the minimum!
This book tries to solve the problem of the poor examples and best practices
that you’ll find proliferating the web.
Other sources
#
Other material from the original author of this book:
HSF CMake Training
Interactive Modern CMake talks
There are some other places to find good information on the web. Here are some of them:
The official help
: Really amazing documentation. Nicely organized, great search, and you can toggle versions at the top. It just doesn’t have a great “best practices tutorial”, which is what this book tries to fill in.
Effective Modern CMake
: A great list of do’s and don’ts.
Embracing Modern CMake
: A post with good description of the term
It’s time to do CMake Right
: A nice set of best practices for Modern CMake projects.
The Ultimate Guide to Modern CMake
: A slightly dated post with similar intent.
More Modern CMake
: A great presentation from Meeting C++ 2018 that recommends CMake 3.12+.

data.title: Benn Jordan's AI poison pill and the weird world of adversarial noise
data.author: glitcher
data.article_summary: Benn Jordan's recent video explores using "adversarial noise poisoning" to protect music from being exploited by generative AI services. This technique exploits the so-called "analog loophole," working wherever sound is heard, and can be adapted to different methods, making it harder for AI to detect and adapt to. Although currently resource-intensive, requiring high-end GPUs and significant electricity, the concept offers a potential way to safeguard music from AI training. The video also discusses related research, such as the HarmonyCloak tool from the University of Tennessee, which similarly aims to protect music. Beyond music, adversarial noise has broader applications in AI defense and attacks, with ongoing research in both offensive and defensive techniques. Despite challenges, such as efficiency and computational demands, this approach opens new possibilities for protecting intellectual property in the age of generative AI.

不同观点：
• **dale_glass** 认为，目前和未来出现的各种模型（如图像和音频模型）本质上都可能成为"蛇油"（意指效果被夸大或无效）。他指出，不同模型的多样性和缺乏文档记录使得攻击或防御它们变得非常困难。此外，新的模型不断出现，现有的防御措施可能很快失效，因此其实际效益有限。

• **Imnimo** 关注使用对抗性扰动来防御GenAI训练的伦理问题。他引用了一篇论文，质疑一些新防御技术的有效性和道德性，认为这些技术可能会误导人们，并不会真正保护他们的作品。

• **janalsncm** 强调了领域专家对机器学习技术的应用，认为随着这些知识的传播，不同领域的实践者会找到实际的解决方案。他将机器学习视作可应用于多种领域的一系列技巧。

• **propter_hoc** 也表达了对Benn Jordan音乐作品的喜爱，但未深入讨论技术问题。

• **KennyBlanken** 则关注讨论中的链接问题，指出应直接链接到原始视频而非博客垃圾。

- **知识产权的伦理和法律问题**：部分用户对版权法在AI模型训练中的适用性和道德性提出质疑，认为需要新的系统来解决这些问题。
- **对Benn Jordan的个人评价**：一些用户表达了对其作品和内容的赞赏，但未深入技术讨论。

争议焦点：
- **对抗性扰动是否是有效的防御手段**，以及这些手段的伦理和法律 implications。
- **版权法在AI模型训练中的适用性**，以及是否需要新的系统来替代现有的版权法。

Benn Jordan’s AI poison pill and the weird world of adversarial noise
Peter Kirn - April 15, 2025
Add comment
Share
Tweet
Benn Jordan’s latest video proposes a way to fight back when generative AI music services rip off music for their data sets. It’s not ready for prime time yet, but it does offer a window into the wild, wonderful world of adversarial noise poisoning attacks.
Now, if you run in circles like mine, you’ve already gotten, “Hey, have you seen this new Benn Jordan video?” already, and I suspect gotten as far as watching it, but here you go:
Benn’s approaches should have some real legs. There are two reasons to be optimistic. One, this family of techniques works on audio, so it covers the so-called “
analog loophole
“: it functions
anywhere
sound is heard. Two, there’s a potential to use
different
methods, thus obfuscating the results. You can also validate the results, meaning these could be updated if services react.
It’s funny; when I spoke to Roland’s Paul McCabe about that company’s AI initiatives, I suggested a speculative design where you could press a button and block a performance from being trained. Benn actually went directly to the data science researchers to find out how that could be done – even in a live instrumental performance.
Of course, you count as a CDM reader if your favorite music in the entire video is the targeted pressure wave attack at 22:00.
The big gotcha – spoiler alert – is that this requires high-end GPUs and a massive amount of electricity and time to pull off. Computation doesn’t magically consume less power on its own, either – least of all with semiconductor trade wars looming. But now that the idea is out there, the challenge would be devising a more efficient method; this at least works as a proof of concept.
In short, I’m for it. And I do expect a fear of training will stop some people from sending music to streaming services. It’s not hard to envision, as Benn does, a world where distributors license this technology to give producers added peace of mind. Remember in the early 2000s when we worried about protecting music from human fans? Now we’re protecting it from generative AI.
It’s worth watching the video, though, because the whole world of adversarial noise gets fascinating – and is a way to imagine hacking increasing AI and surveillance. So this is all about more than just the Poisonify concept (though that’s already essential).
Into the data science
Here’s more on the harmony cloaking tools developed at University of Tennessee Knoxville:
You can’t hear it, but University of Tennessee tool ‘cloaks’ songs to protect music from AI
[
Knoxville News
]
The site/paper also has a survey:
HarmonyCloak: Making Music Unlearnable for Generative AI
The instrument classification attack, as far as I know, is novel.
Even if it didn’t find its market in digital distribution and DSPs, as Benn notes in the video, the AI detection algorithm research Benn did also remains compelling:
Benn Jordan has made an algorithm that can detect if music has been made by AI or not
You’ll find a lot on adversarial noise, in different contexts – because that can be a method of training neural network classifiers and a way of attacking those systems. (There’s “friendly” and “unfriendly,” basically – even though I know that conflicts with what the word “adversarial” normally means. Think of it as “I’m challenging you to a game of chess to teach you something” versus “I’m challenging you to a game of chess to
mind control you
.” Sort of.)
And this stuff is moving

43695401.article_summary: Benn Jordan's recent video explores using "adversarial noise poisoning" to protect music from being exploited by generative AI services. This technique exploits the so-called "analog loophole," working wherever sound is heard, and can be adapted to different methods, making it harder for AI to detect and adapt to. Although currently resource-intensive, requiring high-end GPUs and significant electricity, the concept offers a potential way to safeguard music from AI training. The video also discusses related research, such as the HarmonyCloak tool from the University of Tennessee, which similarly aims to protect music. Beyond music, adversarial noise has broader applications in AI defense and attacks, with ongoing research in both offensive and defensive techniques. Despite challenges, such as efficiency and computational demands, this approach opens new possibilities for protecting intellectual property in the age of generative AI.

data.title: OpenAI is building a social network?
data.author: noleary
data.article_summary: OpenAI正在开发类似X的社交网络，该项目处于早期阶段，内部原型聚焦于ChatGPT的图像生成功能，并包含社交动态。CEO萨姆·奥特曼私下征求外部反馈，但尚未决定是作为独立应用发布还是整合进ChatGPT。此举可能加剧与埃隆·马斯克和马克·扎克伯格的竞争，特别是马斯克曾试图以974亿美元收购OpenAI，而Meta正计划为其AI助手应用添加社交动态。OpenAI的社交应用旨在利用AI帮助用户分享更优质内容，并获取实时数据以训练其AI模型。尽管项目前景不明，但显示出OpenAI在思考扩展业务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI是否应建立社交平台及其潜在价值

不同观点：
• **与《The Culture》类比，强调人际网络的重要性**：  
  [gorgoiler] 认为在一个机器辅助的丰裕世界里，个人的才华不再重要，反而是通过培养人际关系、网络来脱颖而出。未来，现场表演可能成为高收入职业，而传统职业将沦为低收入的副业。

• **AI帮助提升内容质量，但平台充斥垃圾内容**：  
  [beloch] 提出AI可以帮助过滤垃圾内容和虚假信息，创建一个更具人类互动性的平台。然而，担忧这类平台最终会沦为娱乐至死的内容，如名人视频。

• **内容生成器的类型不重要，关键是内容原创性**：  
  [randomor] 认为无论是人类还是AI生成的内容，关键在于内容的原创性。AI可以帮助人类生成更高质量的内容，且可能降低内容生产的摩擦成本。

• **OpenAI可能在构建日常访问的门户而非社交网络**：  
  [tiffanyh] 猜测OpenAI的目标不是传统社交网络，而是类似于过去的Yahoo门户，成为用户每日访问的目的地。

• **社交功能的添加是自然演进**：  
  [frabona] 认为如果OpenAI已经通过ChatGPT生成大量内容，添加轻量级社交功能是保持用户参与的自然步骤，可能成为用户的日常习惯。

• **借鉴Instagram的演变路径**：  
  [mushufasa] 提到Instagram从简单图片分享应用演变为社交网络的例子，认为OpenAI可能会尝试类似的路径，逐步添加社交功能。

• **利用社交数据训练AI**：  
  [rglover] 推测OpenAI可能希望通过获取未加工的社交数据来提升AI的“思考”能力，类似于Elon Musk收购Twitter的动机。

• **LLM原生群聊作为创新社交产品**：  
  [chazeon] 认为基于LLM的群聊可能是非常有趣的产品，因为ChatGPT本身就是一个聊天工具。

• **数据获取作为核心动机**：  
  [pontus] 质疑OpenAI建立社交网络是否只是为了获取更多数据。

• **建立社交网络的挑战在于用户获取**：  
  [Nijikokun] 指出创建社交网络不难，难的是让人们使用它。

• **虚拟朋友和即时满足的社交网络设想**：  
  [janalsncm] 提出一个由AI朋友组成的Facebook式feed，解决用户从零开始建立社交网络的难题，并提供即时满足感。

• **与其他社交网络的比较**：  
  [tomrod] 认为Substack正在构建更具吸引力的社交网络，可能会成为强劲的竞争对手。

补充讨论：
• **AI生成内容可能导致低质量内容泛滥**：  
  [shaftoe444] 认为AI最终可能生成大量低质量内容，导致“内容喂养”现象。

争议焦点：
• OpenAI是否应该建立自己的社交网络，以及该平台的核心价值是提升内容质量还是仅仅获取数据。
